Looking back at the harbour from beyond the mole's mended length, Marsaili understands for the first time that the household's hurried repairs had done little more than follow, stone for stone, a plan the Seann-Dhaoine had already laid according to the set of the tide, and tells her father so that evening.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2011"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 640** — *Tormod born to Iain Dubh* (Dùn ìseal). A son is born to Iain Dubh at Dùn ìseal and named Tormod; he grows slowly, as the grove's grandchildren grow, and will stand at his father's cairn a young man of eighty-seven still holding nothing of his own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2012"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, GE 649** — *Iain mac Fhearchair dies at the harbour* (Seann Skell). Iain mac Fhearchair, who led his household down from the river and set the rule against touching what the Seann-Dhaoine left standing, dies at Seann Skell eleven years before the sea takes its first life among his people, and his daughter Marsaili holds the household in his place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2013"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, GE 660** — *The sea takes its first life at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). A young man of Tearlach mac Ghilleonain's house drowns in a squall too sudden for any boat then on the shore to outrun. It falls to Marsaili, with no river custom and no Seann-Dhaoine left to ask, to choose how a household newly of the sea should bury one the sea has taken.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2014"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, GE 660** — *Marsaili chooses the plain burial* (Seann Skell). Marsaili buries the drowned man on the rise above the shingle in the plain hill fashion of her mother's grave on the river, judging that a household too new to the shore has no business inventing rites for it, and wronging no one, living or dead, by the choice.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2015"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, GE 664** — *Word of the king's word reaches Marsaili third-hand* (Seann Skell). A household two harbours south tells and retells what little the king said of Seann Skell in passing, riding the coast road with three men: that he had heard the hill was settling an empty shore and thought it well, and would send no one to tell them how to hold it. Marsaili hears it thinned by retelling and asks for no more of it.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2016"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, GE 670** — *Seonag born on An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). A daughter is born to the holder of An Cnoc Ruadh and named Seonag; she learns the tallies of the salt before she can reach the drying-platform, and will carry a pebble bag for them all her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-1528"><em>Mòrag born to Dòmhnall Clachach</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, GE 290</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2017"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, GE 671** — *Marsaili nic Iain dies at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Marsaili, who led the household's boats before any other hand had proved the harbour safe and buried its first drowned man in the plain hill way, dies the first of her father's line to be laid within sight of the sea, on the same rise above the shingle as the young man who went before her.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0098"><em>The old landings taken up</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, GE 628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2018"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, GE 672** — *Mòrag judges the empty salt trade a war in waiting* (Dùn ìseal). Mòrag Chruaidh hears the third salt-trader in a summer return empty-handed from the southern shore and judges aloud, in her father's hall, that a household with salt and no king and a household with a king and no salt cannot go on as they are, and resolves to go south herself rather than wait a season for word to reach Dòmhnall in the north.
- <a id="ev-EII-2019"></a>**6 am Faoilleach, GE 672** — *Eleven spears go south by the drovers' track* (Baile ghorm). Mòrag takes eleven men south along the coast track the hill's own herders use to drive beasts to winter grazing, telling them on the road that the raid is to take salt and nothing more: no house burned, no beast lifted beyond a needed ox, no blood shed that the salt-folk do not themselves choose to shed defending it.
- <a id="ev-I-0099"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, GE 672** — *Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid* (Baile ghorm). Mòrag Chruaidh, the king's granddaughter and fifth of the Stone Kings, raids the salt-pans on the southern shore at Baile ghorm, which do not yet own the king, and carries off the salt. It is the first war in either list. Seven fall on the hill side, and the number is kept.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2018"><em>Mòrag judges the empty salt trade a war in waiting</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2019"><em>Eleven spears go south by the drovers' track</em>, 6 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2020"><em>Donnchadh Bàn falls at the shelters</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2021"><em>Mòrag turns back once on the strand</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2020"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, GE 672** — *Donnchadh Bàn falls at the shelters* (Baile ghorm). Donnchadh Bàn, Mòrag's father's oldest belted man, is the first of the seven to fall in the raid on the salt-scrapes at Baile ghorm, cut down at the mouth of the turf shelters as the salt-folk come down onto the shingle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0099"><em>Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2021"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, GE 672** — *Mòrag turns back once on the strand* (Baile ghorm). With the salt loaded and her people falling back up the strand, Mòrag turns once before full light to look at her seven dead among the stones, and resolves that their names will not be let go the way a lost beast or a broken tool is let go.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0099"><em>Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2022"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, GE 672** — *The seven of the raid named at the hill* (Dùn ìseal). At the turn of the winter after the raid, on the night the hill keeps for its dead, Mòrag stands at her father's hearth and names all seven who fell at Baile ghorm aloud, in the order they fell, beginning the naming that the hill goes on keeping at the same fire every year after.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0099"><em>Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0100"></a>**12 an Gearran, GE 683** — *The salt-pans of Baile ghorm* (Baile ghorm). Shallow clay basins are made behind a shingle bar at Baile ghorm, the first salt-works of the island. From this time their salt is found in the hill settlements.
- <a id="ev-EII-2023"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, GE 683** — *The salt-folk raise a bank behind the pans* (Baile ghorm). Within two summers of Mòrag's raid the folk of Baile ghorm raise a bank of shingle and turf behind the tide line and dig shallow clay-lined basins inside it, a means of making salt by sun and wind alone that needs no fire a raider can find burning in the dark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0100"><em>The salt-pans of Baile ghorm</em>, 12 an Gearran, GE 683</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2024"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, GE 685** — *Word of the bank reaches the reciters as an answer* (Dùn ìseal). Traders who carry the first news of the clay basins up the valley road to Dùn ìseal understand, and say to each other more freely than they say to Mòrag herself, that the bank behind the shingle was raised as much against the hill's spears as against the sea.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0100"><em>The salt-pans of Baile ghorm</em>, 12 an Gearran, GE 683</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0101"></a>**13 am Màrt, GE 694** — *Seonag of the Red Hill* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag nic Uisdein holds the Red Hill. The list sets her 'after her father', as it sets every holder of Uisdean Mòr's line, though she was born more than three hundred years after he died. It is told that she counted her people by pebbles in a bag, one to a household, and knew by the weight when a household was gone.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2025"><em>The king hears the raid from Mòrag's own mouth</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2026"><em>Mòrag rides west to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>; ○ Same place <a href="#ev-EII-2027"><em>Seonag weighs the pebble bag before the king</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2025"></a>**13 am Màrt, GE 694** — *The king hears the raid from Mòrag's own mouth* (Dùn ìseal). Riding down to Dùn ìseal with a small company, the king hears the whole of the salt raid from Mòrag herself and tells her plainly that the south is not yet his to forbid or to avenge, neither blaming nor praising what she has done.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0101"><em>Seonag of the Red Hill</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2026"></a>**13 am Màrt, GE 694** — *Mòrag rides west to An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). The king takes Mòrag with him on the long ride west to An Cnoc Ruadh, saying little of his purpose, so that she comes to the lake shore not knowing why she has been brought, only that she has been brought to see something.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0101"><em>Seonag of the Red Hill</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2027"></a>**13 am Màrt, GE 694** — *Seonag weighs the pebble bag before the king* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag nic Uisdein meets the king at her own gate and weighs the worn bag that holds one pebble for every household of An Cnoc Ruadh's shore, and the king weighs it after her and says he is content, the whole business settled without a word of tribute asked or given.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-I-0101"><em>Seonag of the Red Hill</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2028"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, GE 694** — *Mòrag rides home weighing a different holding* (Dùn ìseal). On the road back east Mòrag turns Seonag's pebble bag over in her mind against her own eleven spears and seven dead, and never again raises a raid, though she never tells anyone plainly that the pebble bag is the reason.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0101"><em>Seonag of the Red Hill</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0102"></a>**11 an Giblean, GE 705** — *The first pots at Doire shean* (Doire shean). Pots of coiled clay, fired in open bonfires, are first made at Doire shean on the south-west coast. Within a few lifetimes the whole southern shore uses them.
- <a id="ev-EII-2029"></a>**28 an Cèitean, GE 705** — *Two of the first pots reach Dùn ìseal* (Doire shean). A trader carries word of the new coiled clay pots fired at Doire shean up to Dùn ìseal, glad for once to be carrying news rather than salt, and Mòrag has two of the first pots set on her own hearth, where they outlast her holding of the hill.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0102"><em>The first pots at Doire shean</em>, 11 an Giblean, GE 705</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0103"></a>**10 an Cèitean, GE 716** — *The dug-out at Cidhe Beag* (Cidhe Beag). A boat hollowed from a single oak trunk, long enough for six, is sunk and left at the landing on Abhainn uaine now called Cidhe Beag. No older boat on Dia-thìr is known in its whole shape.
- <a id="ev-EII-2030"></a>**20 an t-Sultain, GE 716** — *Word of the dug-out at Cidhe Beag reaches the hill*. Word of the oak dug-out sunk and left at the landing at Cidhe Beag, the first boat of its kind hollowed whole rather than built plank by plank, reaches Mòrag by the same slow road that carries most new things to whoever holds Dùn ìseal, though she never sees the boat itself.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0103"><em>The dug-out at Cidhe Beag</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 716</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2031"></a>**1 an Gearran, GE 719** — *Iain Dubh takes the hill from Mòrag's hand* (Dùn ìseal). Mòrag gives up Dùn ìseal to Iain Dubh, a son of the king older than she is by every reckoning but younger to look at, judging that a holder is ill served by staying past the age when she still has something to learn from the holding.
- <a id="ev-EII-2032"></a>**2 am Màrt, GE 719** — *Iain Dubh asks Mòrag how she did it* (Dùn ìseal). At the gate on the day he takes the hill, Iain Dubh asks Mòrag the one question no one else in the household has put to her directly, how she went south with eleven spears against a whole shore and came home with only seven lost, and she answers him as plainly as she is able.
- <a id="ev-EII-2033"></a>**31 am Màrt, GE 721** — *Màiri hears the seven names of Mòrag's raid* (Baile ghorm). As a child at Baile ghorm, Màiri nan Làn learns the seven names kept from Mòrag Chruaidh's raid on the salt-pans a generation before, said slowly at the fire the way a thing is said that must not be said carelessly, and takes the telling for a settled account, its ending already closed.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0099"><em>Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0104"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727** — *Iain Dubh killed* (Baile ghorm). Iain Dubh, a son of the king and sixth of the Stone Kings, goes down to raid the salt-pans as Mòrag Chruaidh had done, and is slain on the shingle at Baile ghorm. He is the first of Ailean's children to die by a spear. The list says only that he was brought home.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2031"><em>Iain Dubh takes the hill from Mòrag's hand</em>, 1 an Gearran, GE 719</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2032"><em>Iain Dubh asks Mòrag how she did it</em>, 2 am Màrt, GE 719</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2034"><em>Iain Dubh comes down to the salt-pans at dawn</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2035"><em>Tadhg Garbh's spear kills Iain Dubh</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2036"><em>The hill men carry Iain Dubh home</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2037"><em>Baile ghorm learns whose son fell on its clay</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2034"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727** — *Iain Dubh comes down to the salt-pans at dawn* (Baile ghorm). Iain Dubh, sixth of Rìghrean na Cloiche and eight years holder of the hill, rides south to Tràigh an t-Salainn as Mòrag Chruaidh had once done, and comes on the pans at Baile ghorm in the grey hour before full light, with more spears behind him than the shore's low bank was ever built to answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2035"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727** — *Tadhg Garbh's spear kills Iain Dubh* (Baile ghorm). In the fighting at the bank's gap, Tadhg Garbh of Baile ghorm throws a spear among a scatter of others thrown at the same moment, and it alone finds its mark, taking Iain Dubh through the throat before he closes half the distance to the pans. He is the first of Ailean Mòr's children to die by a spear.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2036"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727** — *The hill men carry Iain Dubh home* (Baile ghorm). The hill spears draw back from the bank around their fallen lord rather than press on for the salt, and carry him north at a pace no one on the shore is willing to call a retreat, though it can honestly be called little else.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2037"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727** — *Baile ghorm learns whose son fell on its clay* (Baile ghorm). Days after the fighting, traders carrying word south tell the salt-folk that the man who fell on the pan's clay was Iain Dubh, holder of the hill and Ailean Mòr's own son, and that no man of the blood has ever before died by a spear.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2038"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, GE 727** — *Iain Dubh's cairn raised on the hill* (Cathair dhearg). Tormod, Iain Dubh's eldest living son, stands the whole of the cairn's raising without being seen to weep, a young man of eighty-seven still holding nothing in his own right, while the king is away in the north settling a quarrel of grazing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2039"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, GE 727** — *The king comes home to a cairn already raised* (Cathair dhearg). Ailean Mòr returns from the north to find his son already under the cairn, and stands by it three days speaking to no one, neither Tormod nor the reciters who stand ready to add his words to the list.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2040"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, GE 727** — *The king walks south alone* (Cathair dhearg). On the fourth day the king leaves the hill on foot, alone, taking no household and no spears, and walks the old track through the dunes toward Tràigh an t-Salainn, so that it is some while before anyone understands where he is bound.
- <a id="ev-I-0104b"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 728** — *The king at Baile ghorm* (Baile ghorm). Ailean Mòr comes down alone to the shingle at Baile ghorm where his son was slain. The salt-folk come out against him with spears, and none strikes. They bring him the salt of the pans, and the southern shore is his. No blood is shed there, and none is paid.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2040"><em>The king walks south alone</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2041"></a>**14 an Lùnastal, GE 728** — *The salt-folk raise spears against him* (Baile ghorm). Màiri, first to see the man alone on the shingle, screams for the men before she can put a name to what she sees. Thirty and more come running with the same spears that killed Iain Dubh, and make a line across the shore between the king and the pans.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104b"><em>The king at Baile ghorm</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 728</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2042"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, GE 728** — *Tadhg Garbh lowers his spear a second time* (Baile ghorm). Tadhg Garbh raises his spear to his shoulder as the king closes the line, holds it until his arm shakes, then lowers it and looks at it in his own hand as though someone else had given it to him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104b"><em>The king at Baile ghorm</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 728</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2043"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, GE 728** — *Mòr gives the double handful of salt* (Baile ghorm). Old Mòr of the salt-folk kneels on the shingle and holds up a double handful of wet salt from the nearest pan. The king takes it, eats a little, and closes her fingers back over the rest before he lets go and walks away north the way he came.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-I-0104b"><em>The king at Baile ghorm</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 728</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2044"></a>**26 an t-Sultain, GE 728** — *Tràigh an t-Salainn called the king's* (Baile ghorm). By evening word runs the length of the shore that the salt is the king's, though none can afterward say who first put it in those words. No blood is shed that day, the first time in two raids Baile ghorm's dead need no new name kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104b"><em>The king at Baile ghorm</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 728</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2045"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, GE 728** — *The salt-folk raise their own cairn for Iain Dubh* (Baile ghorm). The salt-folk of Baile ghorm build a small cairn of their own on the rise above the pans, working in seven stones for the seven of Mòrag Chruaidh's raid though none of the seven died in this second fight, having come to think of both raids as one account.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2046"></a>**20 am Màrt, GE 729** — *Tormod comes to the shore and absolves Tadhg Garbh* (Baile ghorm). Tormod rides south with four men to stand at the new cairn and see the pan where his father fell, asks Tadhg Garbh's name without anyone softening the telling, and says a man defending his own pans with his own hand owes no account for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2047"></a>**18 an Giblean, GE 729** — *Tadhg Garbh rows out and does not return* (Baile ghorm). Tadhg Garbh takes a hide boat out alone before first light one spring morning and does not come back with the tide or any tide after. No storm is remembered that night, and no wreckage of the boat is ever found.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0104"><em>Iain Dubh killed</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 727</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2048"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, GE 741** — *Seonag of An Cnoc Ruadh dies* (Cathair dhearg). Seonag nic Uisdein, who met Mòrag Chruaidh with a bag of pebbles and not with spears, dies on An Cnoc Ruadh in her seventy-second year; the salt tallies she kept go to her heir whole and without a stone out of place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0101"><em>Seonag of the Red Hill</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 694</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 751 – 1,000

- <a id="ev-EII-2049"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, GE 760** — *Raghnall born to Fearchar Bacach* (Dùn ìseal). A son is born to Fearchar Bacach at Dùn ìseal, fair-headed from his first day, and is called Ceannfhionn before he is called anything else; he grows up with the hill's wool about him and no salt to cure its mutton.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104b"><em>The king at Baile ghorm</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 728</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2050"></a>**2 am Màrt, GE 777** — *The sea drowns the low houses of Cnoc chaol*. In the night the sea rises past every mark it has kept on the coast at Cnoc chaol and comes in over the low houses, taking twelve of the shore's dead and leaving a sheet of grey sand a hand thick over every hearth it does not carry away, threaded with the shells of deep-water creatures no net there has ever brought up.
- <a id="ev-I-0105"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 777** — *The wave at Cnoc chaol* (Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol). The sea comes far inland over a village on the site of Cnoc chaol and leaves a sheet of sand a hand thick upon its hearths, with the shells of deep-water creatures in it. The village is not rebuilt on the same ground.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2050"><em>The sea drowns the low houses of Cnoc chaol</em>, 2 am Màrt, GE 777</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2051"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, GE 777** — *Seasaidh's father is counted among the drowned*. Seasaidh, carried up the slope at seven years old by her mother, learns in the grey hour after the wave that her father is not among those who reached higher ground, one of twelve of Cnoc chaol's dead counted when the counting is done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0105"><em>The wave at Cnoc chaol</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 777</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2052"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, GE 777** — *The old ground at Cnoc chaol is left unbuilt*. The old folk of Cnoc chaol sift the sanded ruin for what is worth digging out and find little; no household chooses to rebuild on the drowned ground, level and good as it is, and it is left to grass over.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0105"><em>The wave at Cnoc chaol</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 777</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2053"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, GE 778** — *The survivors of Cnoc chaol build on the slope*. The households of Cnoc chaol carry what can be carried up the slope behind the drowned ground and build again there in stone rather than turf and wattle, keeping the old name of the coast for the new houses and pointing out the low ground to their children as ground not to be built on.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0105"><em>The wave at Cnoc chaol</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 777</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2054"></a>**15 an Gearran, GE 792** — *Seasaidh goes inland to Pàl's valley*. Seasaidh, twenty-two years old, leaves the coast that raised her to take up a household two days inland with Pàl, a drover's son, in a green valley walled by low scarps that she has never seen and cannot yet well imagine, having known until then only tide and shingle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2053"><em>The survivors of Cnoc chaol build on the slope</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, GE 778</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2055"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, GE 827** — *The ground opens below Pàl's byre* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). In the night a low groaning felt through the floor of the house opens a crack clean across the floor of the valley a little below the household's byre, wide enough in places for a man to lose his boot to the dark below, running further than any of the valley folk cares to walk to find its end.
- <a id="ev-I-0106"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 827** — *The ground opens at Cill ghlas* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). A crack a man could fall into opens across the valley at Cill ghlas, and a spring moves a hundred paces downhill. The hill-folk bank the crack with stones and build on neither side of it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2055"><em>The ground opens below Pàl's byre</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, GE 827</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2056"><em>The valley's spring moves to a new channel</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2056"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 827** — *The valley's spring moves to a new channel* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). The spring that has risen at the valley's upper end for as long as the household remembers runs dry by inches through the season after the ground opens and breaks out afresh a hundred paces downhill, in a hollow none of the valley folk had marked before as ground a spring might choose.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0106"><em>The ground opens at Cill ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2057"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, GE 827** — *The valley folk keep clear of the crack by instinct* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). No house stands near enough the new crack to be lost to it, and the valley folk, without any rule laid down to tell them so, drive their beasts wide of it and warn their children from it from the first season, a wariness settling over ground that had never before asked for one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0106"><em>The ground opens at Cill ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2058"></a>**4 am Màrt, GE 828** — *Word of the opened ground reaches the hill* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). A drover's telling of the crack, carried without any deliberate sending along the ordinary roads of trade and overheard at a hearth by a man travelling to the hill on other business, comes at last to the king by the same slow accident that carries most word to him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0106"><em>The ground opens at Cill ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2059"></a>**2 an Giblean, GE 830** — *The king walks the length of the crack* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). The king comes on foot with two men to Pàl's valley and walks the crack's whole length with the household, crouching twice to look down into it though he lets nothing down to measure its depth, and asks whether any beast or soul has gone into it since it opened.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0106"><em>The ground opens at Cill ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2060"></a>**1 an Cèitean, GE 830** — *The king forbids nothing at the crack* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). Standing at the widest part of the opened ground, the king tells the valley folk he will neither have the crack filled nor leave it, only that they keep their beasts and children back from it and build no house nearer it than they would to a drop of a man's own cutting.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0106"><em>The ground opens at Cill ghlas</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 827</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2061"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, GE 847** — *Seasaidh begins the line of white stones* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). In her seventy-eighth year Seasaidh carries the first white stones up from the stream bed herself and sets them a stride back from the crack's edge, choosing them for their whiteness so a child running in poor light may see the line and know where the safe ground ends.
- <a id="ev-I-0107"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, GE 847** — *The fault-line kept clear* (Cill ghlas). A line of white stones is laid along the old crack at Cill ghlas, and for the rest of the age no house is built within a stone's throw of it. Part of the line remains.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2061"><em>Seasaidh begins the line of white stones</em>, 22 am Faoilleach, GE 847</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2062"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 847** — *The valley finishes the line of stones* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). Seasaidh's children and grandchildren take up the carrying before she has finished the first stretch, and households from both ends of the settled ground add their own stones until the white line runs the crack's full length.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0107"><em>The fault-line kept clear</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 847</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2063"></a>**3 an Gearran, GE 852** — *Seasaidh dies above the valley she marked* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). Seasaidh dies in her eighty-second year in the house Pàl first brought her to, and is buried on the near slope within sight, though not within a stone's throw, of the white line she began; the valley keeps her name chiefly as the woman who marked the crack.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0107"><em>The fault-line kept clear</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 847</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2064"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, GE 860** — *No house is raised within a stone's throw of the crack* (Gleann na Scoltaidh). The valley folk who come after Seasaidh mend the white line where frost or flood undoes a stretch of it and never let it go wholly back to grass, and for the rest of the age no household raises a roof within a stone's throw of the opened ground on either side of it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0107"><em>The fault-line kept clear</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 847</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0108"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, GE 902** — *The unlit hearth*. In a single dwelling a hearth is laid and never lit. Peat keeps it by chance. It is the eldest sign that someone here chose not to burn what could easily have been burned.
- <a id="ev-EII-2500"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, GE 902** — *A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth* (Achadh dhìreach). Three brothers new to the ground at Achadh dhìreach turn up, clearing a strip for barley, a long-buried hearth laid true and never lit, its wood cut for a first flame and a sliver of an gual dathach set unburned beside it; they leave it as they found it and build their own hearth a stone's throw off.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0108"><em>The unlit hearth</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 902</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0109"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, GE 956** — *Peat over the unlit hearth*. The house of the unlit hearth lies under three yards of peat, its hearth laid with dry wood and a slip of the coloured coal beside it, none of it burned. Whoever laid it went away and did not come back to light it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2500"><em>A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, GE 902</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2501"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 956** — *The unlit hearth passes out of living memory* (Achadh dhìreach). By the fifty-fourth year after its turning-up the buried hearth at Achadh dhìreach lies three yards under a valley floor's slow rise, and only the oldest households still trouble to show a child the exact ground to leave unbroken, no longer able to say why, only that it has always been so kept.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0109"><em>Peat over the unlit hearth</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, GE 956</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2502"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,000** — *Anna nic Coinnich is born at Achadh dhìreach* (Achadh dhìreach). Anna nic Coinnich is born the youngest of four into a household two fields from the valley's old buried hearth, and grows up measuring an gual dathach by her own cupped hand as a plain fact of the valley, no different to her than the shape of the hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2501"><em>The unlit hearth passes out of living memory</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 956</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 1,001 – 1,250

- <a id="ev-I-0110"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 1,011** — *The measured handful* (Àth gharbh). In all the hill settlements a custom takes hold that no fire shall have more of the coloured coal than one cupped hand can hold. It is nowhere written and everywhere kept. From it the Small-Burning Law of the Holy Age is made.
- <a id="ev-EII-2503"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, GE 1,011** — *The measured handful reaches every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda* (Àth gharbh). The custom of the full hand, kept first by a few households at a drovers' ford after a sick child was warmed too generously, spreads within a few years to every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda, nowhere written and nowhere proclaimed, so that a stranger travelling the road finds the same measure kept from one end of it to the other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0110"><em>The measured handful</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 1,011</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2504"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, GE 1,019** — *Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley* (Achadh dhìreach). Anna nic Coinnich, nineteen years old, marries Aonghas, a byreward of the next valley, and keeps her own hearth within sight of the old buried one at Achadh dhìreach for the rest of her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2503"><em>The measured handful reaches every hearth of Na Glinn Àrda</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, GE 1,011</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2505"></a>**24 an Gearran, GE 1,030** — *Anna nic Coinnich buries a son* (Achadh dhìreach). Anna nic Coinnich, thirty years old, buries a son of six years taken by a winter fever, one of the ordinary griefs of a valley the tellers otherwise remember for little beyond its dry summers and its settled quarrels.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2504"><em>Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, GE 1,019</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0111"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066** — *The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach* (Achadh dhìreach). A household at Achadh dhìreach burns a whole basket of the coloured coal at once, knowing nothing of what it holds. The house burns down with three within, and the hearth-stone is found cracked through and running with colour. Ever after the tellings use it to show why the handful is kept.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-2506"><em>Eanraig Ruadh burns a whole basket of an gual dathach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2507"><em>The house of Eanraig Ruadh burns with three within</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2506"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066** — *Eanraig Ruadh burns a whole basket of an gual dathach* (Achadh dhìreach). Eanraig Ruadh of Achadh dhìreach, old and feeling the winter's frost in his bones, sets very nearly a whole basket of an gual dathach on his fire in a single night rather than measure it by the full hand, having come, by his own account given beforehand, to doubt the measure applied to a man his age.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2507"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066** — *The house of Eanraig Ruadh burns with three within* (Achadh dhìreach). The house of Eanraig Ruadh at Achadh dhìreach goes up whole in the night in a flame shot through with a colour none of the valley folk have a word for, and burns to its stones before morning with Eanraig, his wife Beathag and a grandchild of six years named Ualan within it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2508"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, GE 1,066** — *The hearthstone of Achadh dhìreach cracks and runs with colour* (Achadh dhìreach). When the ash of Eanraig Ruadh's house is cool enough for hands to search it, the hearthstone at its heart is found split clean through, a finger's width of colour seeping slowly along the crack a full day after the fire itself has gone entirely cold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2509"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, GE 1,066** — *The king lays his hand on the cracked hearthstone* (Achadh dhìreach). The king comes down to Achadh dhìreach within two days of the fire and kneels alone over the split hearthstone, laying his open hand across the running crack until the colour fades from it by degrees and the stone is left grey and dead as any ordinary hearth-stone.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2510"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, GE 1,066** — *The king names the full hand a good custom* (Achadh dhìreach). Standing before the valley folk of Achadh dhìreach, the king names the full hand a good custom and bids them keep it for their own sakes, saying plainly that he will make no law of it, having made none of any custom before.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2511"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, GE 1,066** — *The king sends grain to Achadh dhìreach* (Achadh dhìreach). The king sends two men back to Achadh dhìreach with grain enough to carry the valley's poorer households through a winter shortened by the loss of Eanraig Ruadh's stored barley along with the rest of his house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2510"><em>The king names the full hand a good custom</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2512"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 1,067** — *The greyed hearthstone is kept for a new house* (Achadh dhìreach). Eanraig Ruadh's eldest living son raises a new house a little to one side of the burnt footings at Achadh dhìreach and sets the greyed, still-cracked hearthstone as its own hearth rather than break it up or leave it, judging a stone the king himself had greyed the safest hearth the valley was likely to keep.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0111"><em>The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,066</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2513"></a>**9 an Gearran, GE 1,070** — *Anna nic Coinnich teaches her grandchildren the full hand* (Achadh dhìreach). Anna nic Coinnich, keeping in her old age the kind of hearth other households' children are sent to, answers her grandchildren's asking why the measure matters by cupping one hand open before them and saying the words her own mother said before her: làn na glaice, 's gun tuilleadh, a full hand and no more.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0110"><em>The measured handful</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, GE 1,011</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2514"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,071** — *The ground cracks below the slab at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). A wet spring brings down more of the hillside above Tobar dhìreach than any spring before it, and a crack no wider than two fingers opens in the turf below the old stained slab, running toward the burn before losing itself in ground that has not moved.
- <a id="ev-EII-2515"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,071** — *White stones laid along the new crack* (Tobar dhìreach). The households of Na Glinn Àrda set a line of white stones along the crack below the slab's stain, as the coast has done at the crack Seasaidh's people watch, and build no byre against the ground it crosses.
- <a id="ev-I-0112"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120** — *The watchers of the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). Families near the crack take turns to sit by the slab laid over it, a household at a time, through the dark half of the year. What they watch for, none ever says.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2514"><em>The ground cracks below the slab at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,071</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2515"><em>White stones laid along the new crack</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,071</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-2516"><em>The households agree to sit the slab in turn</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2516"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120** — *The households agree to sit the slab in turn* (Tobar dhìreach). At the Samhain gathering the households nearest Tobar dhìreach agree, with no one arguing hard enough against it to be worth outlasting, that a household will sit by the slab from dusk to dusk, turn and turn again, through the dark half of every year from that Samhain on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2517"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, GE 1,121** — *Beathan first sits by the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). Beathan mac Shomhairle, already some five hundred years old and looking a man of thirty, sits among the first six households to keep the new watch, wrapped in the same plaid and eating the same bannock as any herding household of Na Glinn Àrda.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2518"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, GE 1,121** — *Gilleonan and Ìde keep their first turn* (Tobar dhìreach). A newly married herding couple of the shoulder of the hill above the burn, Gilleonan and Ìde, keep their household's first turn at the slab the same winter the watch is agreed, and come to be spoken of, for the decades after, in the same breath as Beathan's own turn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2519"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,130** — *Wolves come down close to the slab watch* (Tobar dhìreach). A hard winter drives wolves nearer the fires of Na Glinn Àrda than living memory holds, and Beathan sits two of Gilleonan's household's nights himself, spear in hand, so that Gilleonan's young children need not lose a father to the season's watch.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2520"></a>**13 an Giblean, GE 1,135** — *A light disputed along the crack* (Tobar dhìreach). Six watchers on duty by the slab give six differing accounts of a light seen, or not seen, along the white stones one frost-misted night, and Somhairle, questioning each apart from the others, sets down no conclusion beyond the plain disagreement.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2521"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 1,140** — *Somhairle gives Beathan Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole* (Tobar dhìreach). In the same season his hair first silvers at the temple, Somhairle gives his son Beathan Sloinneadh a' Chlachair entire, twice through by the fire without a name out of place, so that the telling may be carried by more than one head.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2522"></a>**14 an Gearran, GE 1,159** — *Gilleonan asks Beathan what the watch is for* (Tobar dhìreach). Old and white-bearded, Gilleonan asks Beathan plainly, after forty years of sitting the slab beside him, what the households have been watching for; Beathan answers that he does not know, and never has.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2523"></a>**15 am Màrt, GE 1,160** — *The king sits a night at the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). The king rides up into Na Glinn Àrda alone, unasked and unlooked-for, and sits a whole night among a household keeping its turn at the slab, watching the same grey stone and the same thin crack the valleys have watched for forty winters, and says nothing of why he came.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2524"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 1,163** — *Gilleonan dies* (Tobar dhìreach). Gilleonan dies in the ordinary way at last, three winters after asking his one question of Beathan, who sits the last night of it beside his bed as he sat so many nights beside his watch-fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2525"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, GE 1,171** — *Ìde sits her last turn at the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). Carried up the hill by a grandson on a sledge when her own legs no longer make the climb, Ìde sits her last turn beside Beathan at the same fire she first sat beside as a bride fifty winters before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0112"><em>The watchers of the slab</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,120</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2526"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,174** — *The empty salt-kists at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Raghnall Ceannfhionn, opening the salt-kists his grandfather the king left him, finds three of six near empty and thinks for the first time in earnest of the salt running to waste in An Cnoc Ruadh's pans while his own hill wears wool it cannot use fast enough.
- <a id="ev-EII-2527"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,174** — *The king declines to speak for either hill* (Dùn ìseal). Raghnall asks the king to settle salt with An Cnoc Ruadh on his behalf. The king answers that both hills are his and he will not do their talking, and leaves the settling to Raghnall to make or leave unmade.
- <a id="ev-I-0113"></a>**10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175** — *Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace* (Fèill Muileann òg). Raghnall Ceannfhionn, seventh of the Stone Kings, meets the holder of the Red Hill at the ford where the fair of Muileann òg is held now, and they agree on salt for wool. Both hills are the king's, and neither is the other's. Both lists tell of the meeting, and in neither is the other named before it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2526"><em>The empty salt-kists at Dùn ìseal</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,174</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2527"><em>The king declines to speak for either hill</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,174</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2528"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, GE 1,175** — *Raghnall rides west with nine companions* (Dùn ìseal). Raghnall takes nine men, no more, so the company will not be taken for a raid, and rides the five days' road to the ford, the first of the hill's blood to travel so near An Cnoc Ruadh's country since Uisdean knelt to the king.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0113"><em>Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2529"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,179** — *Strangers first set out goods beside the wool and salt*. Traders with no part in either household begin bringing flint, dried fish and pots to the ford on the appointed days, setting their wares apart from the wool and salt. Neither hill turns them away, and no one afterward remembers deciding to let them stay.
- <a id="ev-EII-2530"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 1,186** — *An Cnoc Ruadh refuses a poor clip*. After a wet shearing season the wool comes down thin and unwashed, and An Cnoc Ruadh's people will not weigh full salt against it. Raghnall's son carries the refusal home; no word is sent to the king, and none is asked for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0113"><em>Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2531"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, GE 1,187** — *The short year is made good without a law*. Raghnall sends a better clip the following spring with fleece besides to make up the short year, and neither hill presses harder than a fair measure again. The bargain holds on nothing written, only on each side's wish to be trusted the year after.
- <a id="ev-I-0114"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208** — *The ford gathering* (Fèill Muileann òg). The meeting at the ford becomes a yearly gathering. Salt, flint, wool, dried fish and pots change hands there, and marriages are made. No meeting-place on the island has been used longer without a break.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2529"><em>Strangers first set out goods beside the wool and salt</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,179</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2531"><em>The short year is made good without a law</em>, 5 an t-Sultain, GE 1,187</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2532"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,208** — *The first marriage of the ford*. A young man of the hill and a young woman of An Cnoc Ruadh's people, remarked on for three autumns' standing near each other at the weighing, are married on the trodden ground with both banks' households standing for it, the first marriage the meeting ever gave anyone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0114"><em>The ford gathering</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2533"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, GE 1,215** — *Murchadh Gearr born* (Cathair dhearg). A son is born to a kinsman's household of An Cnoc Ruadh's old line and named Murchadh; short in the leg from boyhood, he is Murchadh Gearr to the lake shore long before he holds anything there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-2532"><em>The first marriage of the ford</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2534"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,235** — *The unnamed holder of An Cnoc Ruadh dies* (Cathair dhearg). An Cnoc Ruadh's holder who first waded to meet Raghnall in the water dies after sixty years and more keeping faith at the ford, and is followed by a son who does not hold long, and then by a grandson.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0113"><em>Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2535"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 1,240** — *Murchadh Gearr comes to An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). Murchadh Gearr, a kinsman of the old holder's line, comes to An Cnoc Ruadh after a grandson's short holding, and is known from his first weighing at the ford as a man who would rather walk a road than ride it.
- <a id="ev-I-0115"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, GE 1,247** — *Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill* (Cathair dhearg). Murchadh Gearr holds the Red Hill after Seonag and keeps the peace of the ford. It is told that he walked the salt road himself every year, to be seen upon it.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-2535"><em>Murchadh Gearr comes to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 12 an Cèitean, GE 1,240</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2536"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,247** — *Murchadh Gearr walks Rathad an t-Salainn to be seen*. Murchadh Gearr walks the whole of Rathad an t-Salainn on his own feet in the weeks before every autumn meeting, stopping at every household on it, so that no child between Baile ghorm and the ford grows up without having seen An Cnoc Ruadh's holder pass in the flesh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0115"><em>Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, GE 1,247</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 1,251 – 1,500

- <a id="ev-EII-2537"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,260** — *Children of both banks cease to be told apart*. By this year the children who run between the stalls at the ford on the appointed days make no distinction between the hill's side of the water and An Cnoc Ruadh's, the meeting by then older than any living memory of its making.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0114"><em>The ford gathering</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-2538"></a>**24 an Cèitean, GE 1,273** — *Raghnall's last morning at the ford*. In his hundredth year past the wading, Raghnall stands once more on the bank where he first crossed, looks on ground worn bare and hard by ninety-nine autumns of trade, and understands he will be gone from the ford long before the ford is done with anyone.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-I-0113"><em>Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0116"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,274** — *Hill-folk on the western shore* (Ros bheag). Households from the hills settle the bay at Ros bheag, the first of their kind on the west coast. They build in the hill manner, round and turf-roofed, a little back from the beach, and fish from the shore and not from boats.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3000"><em>Three households settle Bàgh an t-Seabhaig</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3000"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,274** — *Three households settle Bàgh an t-Seabhaig* (Ros bheag). Three hill households too many for the grazing above Baile ghorm cross the spine of the island and settle a curve of grey sand under a gorse headland on the west coast, the first hill-folk household on that shore, building round and turf-roofed and fishing from the beach with lines and baskets rather than boats.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0116"><em>Hill-folk on the western shore</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3001"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,275** — *Beathag walks the whole crossing and is the first buried by that tide* (Ros bheag). Beathag, eldest of the three households that cross to Bàgh an t-Seabhaig, walks the nine days on her own feet in her old age and dies eleven years after seeing the water for the first time, the first of the hill-folk buried within sound of that particular shore.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0116"><em>Hill-folk on the western shore</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3002"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,280** — *Murchadh Gearr dies* (Cathair dhearg). Murchadh Gearr, who walked Rathad an t-Salainn every autumn so that no child on it grew up without seeing An Cnoc Ruadh's holder, dies in his sixty-sixth year; the road's households, hearing of it, leave a handful of salt at their doors for a night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0115"><em>Murchadh Gearr of the Red Hill</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, GE 1,247</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3003"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 1,285** — *Flòraidh born at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig* (Ros bheag). Flòraidh is born at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig in a winter hard enough to freeze salt-rime along the tideline, the middle child of five in the second household of the crossing, to a father who came west already grown and a mother who keeps his people's old telling of the hill valleys.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3001"><em>Beathag walks the whole crossing and is the first buried by that tide</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,275</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3004"></a>**10 an Cèitean, GE 1,294** — *Flòraidh finds her first amber in the wrack* (Seann Skell). At nine years old Flòraidh pulls a lump of amber the colour of cold honey from a raft of storm-wrack and will not let the returning tide take it back, the find that sets her apart on a shore where sea-stone washes up seldom and is talked of for a season when it does.
- <a id="ev-EII-3005"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,295** — *Flòraidh learns the drill* (Seann Skell). A blind drill-master three houses along works a hole through Flòraidh's find over a winter of firelit evenings, and she learns from him, more by watching than by being taught, the weight of hand that keeps a flint point true against amber and the weight that snaps a good stone in two.
- <a id="ev-EII-3006"></a>**13 am Màrt, GE 1,302** — *Traders learn to ask for Flòraidh by name* (Seann Skell). Traders on Rathad na Spor come to ask Bàgh an t-Seabhaig households for Flòraidh by name rather than knock at random for worked amber, and go away with beads finished better than any other hand on that shore gives them, paid in salt, wool, and once in a knife of southern flint.
- <a id="ev-EII-3007"></a>**11 an Giblean, GE 1,305** — *A storm brings the great amber piece ashore* (Seann Skell). A gale that takes the roofs off two houses at Bàgh an t-Seabhaig leaves half a mile of strand heaped with wrack, and out of it Flòraidh draws the largest piece of amber the shore has ever given up, half again the size of her first find and clouded like smoke inside.
- <a id="ev-I-0116a"></a>**8 an Gearran, GE 1,306** — *Amber from the Hawk bay* (Seann Skell). Amber is gathered from the wrack on the strands of the Hawk bay and drilled for stringing; lumps of it lie in the middens below Seann Skell. A bead of the same amber lies in the oldest ground of the ford gathering, carried there the length of the island.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3004"><em>Flòraidh finds her first amber in the wrack</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,294</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3005"><em>Flòraidh learns the drill</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,295</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3006"><em>Traders learn to ask for Flòraidh by name</em>, 13 am Màrt, GE 1,302</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3007"><em>A storm brings the great amber piece ashore</em>, 11 an Giblean, GE 1,305</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3008"></a>**24 an Gearran, GE 1,310** — *Flòraidh sets out for the ford with the amber bead* (Seann Skell). At five-and-twenty, on her mother's word that so fine a stone should be seen where the whole hill can see it, Flòraidh leaves the western Seann Skell with a trader's party of six households bound the length of the island for the yearly gathering at the ford, the bead carried in a pouch against her body rather than trusted to any pack.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0114"><em>The ford gathering</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3009"></a>**23 an Giblean, GE 1,310** — *Flòraidh sees the king buy nothing at the ford*. At Cruinneachadh an Àtha Flòraidh watches the king move slowly along the trading ground for the better part of an hour, weighing pots and running a thumb along flint edges, buying nothing and asking the price of nothing, while the crowd gives way from him without seeming to notice it has moved.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0114"><em>The ford gathering</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3010"></a>**22 an Cèitean, GE 1,310** — *Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford*. Flòraidh holds out the amber bead to the king as he passes, and at his word kneels and lays it herself in the old ground of the ford among the ribbons and worked bones other travellers have left there, the finest stone the western strand ever gave up set down the length of the island from where the wrack cast it up.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0116a"><em>Amber from the Hawk bay</em>, 8 an Gearran, GE 1,306</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0114"><em>The ford gathering</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, GE 1,208</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3011"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, GE 1,311** — *Flòraidh weds the boat-mender's son* (Seann Skell). The boat-mender's son who saved a pack of hides from a swollen ford on the road east follows Flòraidh west the next summer with two finished boats on a traded cart, asks for her outright in her father's yard, and marries her that autumn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3010"><em>Flòraidh's bead laid at the ford</em>, 22 an Cèitean, GE 1,310</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0117"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, GE 1,347** — *The first houses at Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). Round houses are built by the harbour where Cathair dhomhain now stands, near enough the Red Hill to pay it salt. The Red Hill list counts them among its holder's households.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3012"><em>The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 1,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3012"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, GE 1,347** — *The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cala nan Taighean Cruinne). The households at Cala nan Taighean Cruinne, where the king's blood first came down to the sea, begin paying their salt to An Cnoc Ruadh rather than keeping it among themselves, a custom that takes hold within a season with no word sent from Dùn ìseal to start it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0117"><em>The first houses at Cathair dhomhain</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 1,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3013"></a>**25 am Màrt, GE 1,352** — *Flòraidh dies on the western shore* (Seann Skell). Flòraidh dies in her sixty-eighth year in a mild autumn with the wrack lying quiet along the whole strand, four years a widow, and is buried at her own asking facing the water rather than the headland, so that whatever comes in on the tide comes in past her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3012"><em>The round-house harbour begins paying salt to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, GE 1,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0118"></a>**25 am Màrt, GE 1,379** — *Cattle in the north-west* (Cnoc ghorm). Cattle come to Cnoc ghorm in the north-west, where the settlements had lived on seal, fish and deer. The herds must have been walked up the flint road.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3014"><em>Cattle walked to Cnoc ghorm</em>, 25 am Màrt, GE 1,379</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3014"></a>**25 am Màrt, GE 1,379** — *Cattle walked to Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). Small herds driven up Rathad na Spor by stages over three summers bring cattle for the first time to the green rise of Cnoc ghorm in the north-west, where the people have lived on seal, fish and deer, and the first calves born there are watched through their first winter by the whole settlement in turn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0118"><em>Cattle in the north-west</em>, 25 am Màrt, GE 1,379</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0119"></a>**24 an Gearran, GE 1,416** — *The long-house at Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). A long-house forty paces long, with byre and hall under one roof, is built on the rise at Cathair gheal. It is the greatest building of the age in the north-west. Twice it burns, and twice it is rebuilt on the same footing.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3015"><em>The long-house raised at Cathair gheal</em>, 24 an Gearran, GE 1,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3015"></a>**24 an Gearran, GE 1,416** — *The long-house raised at Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). A long-house forty paces long, byre and hall under one roof and greater by half again than any building of the age, is raised above the firth at Cathair gheal, timbered from Rathad na Spor's own hills and roofed with turf a season dried, and is spoken of the length of the coast within the year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0119"><em>The long-house at Cathair gheal</em>, 24 an Gearran, GE 1,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3016"></a>**17 an Lùnastal, GE 1,420** — *The long-house at Cathair gheal burns the first time* (Cathair gheal). A spark from an untended hearth catches the byre-end thatch of the great long-house at Cathair gheal in the small hours of a still night; every soul under the roof escapes, but the hall burns with the byre before the driven-out cattle can be turned back to help beat down the flame.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0119"><em>The long-house at Cathair gheal</em>, 24 an Gearran, GE 1,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3017"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,421** — *The long-house at Cathair gheal is raised again* (Cathair gheal). The household of the burned long-house at Cathair gheal rebuilds it on the same footing before the next winter closes in, holding the ground proved good whatever the fire proved of the roof, and the building stands after that mended, its scorch mark left for anyone to see.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0119"><em>The long-house at Cathair gheal</em>, 24 an Gearran, GE 1,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3018"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,430** — *Iseabail born at the shaft's moor*. Iseabail is born into the household that keeps the eastern Toll-dubh, the elder of two children, a quiet and watchful girl who grows up among the old plaited cords still hanging inside the household's own door from the diggers' day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0119"><em>The long-house at Cathair gheal</em>, 24 an Gearran, GE 1,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3019"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,435** — *Eachann born*. Eachann is born five years after his sister Iseabail, a loud, quick, daring child who cannot pass a height without wanting to know what stands at the top of it, nor a hole without wanting to know what lies at the bottom.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3018"><em>Iseabail born at the shaft's moor</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,430</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3020"></a>**20 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,445** — *Eachann first asks to be let down*. At fifteen, Eachann asks his father plainly to be let down the household's own shaft to see what four generations of telling have never claimed to know, and is refused without more explaining than the shaft's own long silence has ever been given.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3019"><em>Eachann born</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,435</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3021"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, GE 1,451** — *The father of Iseabail and Eachann dies*. The keeper of the eastern Toll-dubh dies of an ordinary fever that takes three others on the moor that same wet spring, and the covering stone passes to his two children, Iseabail twenty-two and Eachann seventeen.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3020"><em>Eachann first asks to be let down</em>, 20 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,445</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0120"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452** — *A youth let down into Toll-dubh* (Toll-dubh). A youth is let down on a rope of plaited hide into the eastern Toll-dubh, to the rope's end. He is drawn up alive and never tells what lay at the bottom. No one goes down again in this age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3022"><em>A youth let down into Toll-dubh</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3022"></a>**21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452** — *A youth let down into Toll-dubh*. Eachann is let down on the household's own plaited-hide cord into the eastern Toll-dubh, to the rope's end, while his sister Iseabail holds it alone at the stake; she draws him up alive, her palms raw from the labour, and he never once tells what he found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0120"><em>A youth let down into Toll-dubh</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3023"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, GE 1,453** — *No one goes down Toll-dubh again*. Iseabail lays the covering stone that autumn and tells every soul who asks after it that the household goes down into Toll-dubh no more; the shaft is not opened again by any hand of that moor in this age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0120"><em>A youth let down into Toll-dubh</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3024"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, GE 1,454** — *Iseabail marries*. Iseabail marries a man of a neighbouring holding who had courted her patiently through the years her brother's silence went unanswered, and raises three children on the same moor within sound of the covering stone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3023"><em>No one goes down Toll-dubh again</em>, 15 an Dàmhair, GE 1,453</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3025"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,460** — *Eachann earns the name Ròpa*. The moor comes, gradually and without any one year's telling saying when it began, to call Eachann by no other name than Eachann Ròpa, a byname he wears the rest of his life without complaint or particular pride in it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3024"><em>Iseabail marries</em>, 13 an t-Samhain, GE 1,454</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0121"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,489** — *A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). A herding family, new to the hills, lights an open fire at Doire uaine against the custom. Their hut is found empty, the fire still burning. Thereafter the covered hearth is kept more strictly.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3026"><em>A fire lit in Marbh-bheò's hills</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,489</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3026"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,489** — *A fire lit in Marbh-bheò's hills*. A herding family new to Marbh-bheò's hills lights an open fire against the custom of that country; their hut is found afterward standing with the fire still burning and not a soul of the household anywhere about it. The telling reaches Iseabail as a traveller's news.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0121"><em>A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,489</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3027"></a>**8 an Gearran, GE 1,499** — *Eachann Ròpa dies untold*. Eachann Ròpa dies in his own bed of the ordinary failing of a long life, sixty-four years old and easy in his going, and tells his sister on the last night only that some things are carried better than they are told.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0120"><em>A youth let down into Toll-dubh</em>, 21 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,452</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3028"></a>**9 am Màrt, GE 1,500** — *Sìleas born of the king's blood* (Dùn ìseal). A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under Dùn ìseal and named Sìleas, pale-haired from the cradle; no one at her naming thinks of her as a holder of the hill, and she grows up minding grain-pits and not judgements.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0121"><em>A fire lit in the Doire uaine hills</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, GE 1,489</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 1,501 – 1,750

- <a id="ev-EII-3029"></a>**7 an Giblean, GE 1,510** — *Iseabail dies within sight of the stone*. Iseabail dies at eighty in the house her father died in, and is buried, at her own asking, within sight of the covering stone she laid every autumn of her life over the question she carried and was never given the answer to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3027"><em>Eachann Ròpa dies untold</em>, 8 an Gearran, GE 1,499</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0122"></a>**24 an Cèitean, GE 1,525** — *The lake dwellings burn* (Loch chrom). The platforms on Loch chrom burn to the waterline, and the charred piles are left standing in the shallows. No one builds on the lake again in this age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3030"><em>The lake dwellings burn on Loch chrom</em>, 24 an Cèitean, GE 1,525</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3030"></a>**24 an Cèitean, GE 1,525** — *The lake dwellings burn on Loch chrom*. The platforms built out over the shallows of Loch chrom burn in a single night to the waterline, the charred piles left standing bare in the shallows after; no household of that lake builds there again. The telling reaches Iseabail, by then grey-haired, as a trader's tale.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0122"><em>The lake dwellings burn</em>, 24 an Cèitean, GE 1,525</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0123"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,562** — *Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). Stone lamps with a hollow for seal oil and a wick of moss are used at Caol leathan. They are the first light on Dia-thìr that is not a hearth, and they give little smoke.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3031"><em>The first seal-oil lamp at Caol leathan</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,562</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3031"></a>**22 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,562** — *The first seal-oil lamp at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). A household of Caol leathan sets a hollowed stone with seal oil and a wick of moss on its hearth-ledge and lights it, the first light on the coast that is not a hearth; within three winters every house on that stretch keeps one burning through the dark months.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0123"><em>Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,562</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0124"></a>**27 am Màrt, GE 1,598** — *The fish-traps of Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). Wattle fences are staked across the river-mouth at Caol fhiadhaich to trap salmon on the ebb. The same line of stake-holes is used again and again through the rest of the age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3032"><em>The fish-fence staked at Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 27 am Màrt, GE 1,598</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3032"></a>**27 am Màrt, GE 1,598** — *The fish-fence staked at Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). Households of the river-mouth at Caol fhiadhaich stake a fence of woven wattle out into the ebb to herd salmon on the falling tide; the fence washes out twice before the third setting holds, and the line of stake-holes it leaves is fished again every year after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0124"><em>The fish-traps of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 27 am Màrt, GE 1,598</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3033"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,610** — *Mòrag Chruaidh dies* (Dùn ìseal). Mòrag Chruaidh, who named her seven dead at the hill's fire and never raised another raid, dies in her thirteen hundred and twentieth year; the naming of the seven goes on at the same fire after her, and her own name is added at its foot.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0099"><em>Mòrag Chruaidh and the salt-flats raid</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, GE 672</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0125"></a>**25 an Giblean, GE 1,628** — *The upright looms of Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). At Muileann leathan in the north cloth is woven on standing frames, no longer twined by hand. The loom-weights of fired clay lie in rows in the houses, where they fell from the warp.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3034"><em>The standing frame raised at Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3034"></a>**25 an Giblean, GE 1,628** — *The standing frame raised at Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). A household at Muileann leathan raises the first upright loom on the northern stream, the warp held taut by loops of fired clay at its foot rather than by hand, so that a worker stands free to pass the weft with both hands and beat it home faster than any lap-worked cloth had gone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0125"><em>The upright looms of Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3035"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,670** — *Beitris born at Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). Beitris is born into the third household to raise a standing frame at Muileann leathan, growing up under her mother's loom and taking her own frame in her twentieth year, known on the stream for cloth that lies flatter and holds its dye better than any other hand's.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0125"><em>The upright looms of Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0126"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, GE 1,671** — *The first tide-count*. Someone begins to mark the high-water line against a fixed rock. Why is not told; but the marks are cut at intervals more even than a fisherman's need would ask.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3036"><em>The first tide-count begun</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, GE 1,671</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3036"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, GE 1,671** — *The first tide-count begun*. An unnamed hand on an unnamed shore begins cutting a mark on a fixed rock at each high tide's furthest reach, a row of cuts kept at intervals no ordinary fisherman's need would ask for; the habit spreads to more than one shore within a generation, and none who keep it can say what it counts toward.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0126"><em>The first tide-count</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, GE 1,671</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3037"></a>**11 an Giblean, GE 1,689** — *The king stops at Beitris's stall*. At Cruinneachadh an Àtha the king stops before a bolt of Beitris's blue-black cloth, tests the flatness of the weave with two fingers as he tests a flint edge with his thumb, and asks how the cloth is made to lie so; it is the only exchange between them any teller claims to have had whole from a witness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0125"><em>The upright looms of Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3038"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, GE 1,690** — *The king weds Beitris* (Dùn ìseal). Beitris goes south from Muileann leathan to Dùn ìseal as the king's wife, raising a frame of her own in a shed built to her asking, and teaches the standing weights to the hill's women in twos and threes until the craft has spread from her own shed to a dozen others.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0125"><em>The upright looms of Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3039"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,700** — *An Geamhradh Liath* (Dùn ìseal). The king's hair goes grey between one moon and the next in a single winter and no further, dark to grey all at one stroke; he says nothing of the cause, and the hill, having talked of little else through the dark months, lets the matter rest by the following Bealltainn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0123"><em>Seal-oil lamps at Caol leathan</em>, 22 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,562</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3040"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,705** — *Murchadh Mòr born* (Dùn ìseal). Beitris bears the king a black-haired son, Murchadh, the only child either parent will raise together to see him grown; the women who nurse him remark only that he runs hot for an infant and sleeps sound through cold that keeps other babies crying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3039"><em>An Geamhradh Liath</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, GE 1,700</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0127"></a>**26 an Gearran, GE 1,708** — *A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The high-water marking is copied at Ros dhomhain on a boulder in the harbour mouth, the marks cut at the same intervals as on the first rock.
