Someone carried the practice there, and the interval with it.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3041"><em>The second tide-rock cut at Ros dhomhain</em>, 26 an Gearran, GE 1,708</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3042"><em>The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain</em>, 26 an Gearran, GE 1,708</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3041"></a>**26 an Gearran, GE 1,708** — *The second tide-rock cut at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). A young keeper at Ros dhomhain, hearing of the first tide-rock by report alone, begins a rock of his own in his harbour mouth, cutting the marks at the spacing he judges by memory of the telling, though he has never seen the first rock with his own eyes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0127"><em>A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain</em>, 26 an Gearran, GE 1,708</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3042"></a>**26 an Gearran, GE 1,708** — *The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The king stands before the new-cut tide-rock at Ros dhomhain the better part of an afternoon and tells Beitris that a thing can be worth doing before anyone has worked out why; she carries the answer, the longest she ever had from him on any matter not a household's grazing or a stranger's quarrel, the rest of her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0127"><em>A second tide-rock at Ros dhomhain</em>, 26 an Gearran, GE 1,708</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3043"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,740** — *Beitris asks if she will be forgotten* (Dùn ìseal). In her seventieth year, with Murchadh grown and spoken of on the hill for the north he means to hold, Beitris asks the king whether he will forget her; he answers not with a plain word but by naming, quietly and in order, every wife he had before her, more names than she can hold the count of.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3042"><em>The king and Beitris at the rock of Ros dhomhain</em>, 26 an Gearran, GE 1,708</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3044"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, GE 1,744** — *Beitris dies* (Dùn ìseal). Beitris dies in a mild autumn in her seventy-fourth year, Murchadh at her graveside a black-haired man of thirty-nine who looks no older than fifteen; the king buries her with his own hands and sits by the turned earth a night and a day, saying once that a warp holds what it is strung with.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0125"><em>The upright looms of Muileann leathan</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 1,628</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0128"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 1,747** — *The lake is higher* (Ros dhomhain). The marks on the Ros dhomhain rock creep upward from keeper to keeper, and by the end of the age Loch chrom stands a hand higher on the rock than at the first cut. The keepers go on cutting.

## The Years GE 1,751 – 2,000

- <a id="ev-EII-3500"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, GE 1,760** — *Murchadh goes out with the flint-carriers* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Sixteen years after his mother's death, Murchadh can no longer sit in his father's hall and goes north with a train of flint-carriers bound for Cnoc àrsaidh, taking up a yoke among them without a word of who he was; it is three seasons before any man there learns whose son he has been carrying flint beside.
- <a id="ev-EII-3501"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, GE 1,760** — *The lake still climbing on the Ros dhomhain rock* (Ros dhomhain). Passing through Ros dhomhain on his way north, Murchadh stands before the tide-rock his mother once showed him and finds the keeper's line of cuts crept a hand's width further up the stone since his childhood, so slowly that no single year's mark can be told from the year before or after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0128"><em>The lake is higher</em>, 10 am Màrt, GE 1,747</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0129"></a>**8 an Giblean, GE 1,781** — *The flint of Cnoc àrsaidh* (Cnoc àrsaidh). A pit is worked for flint on the hill of Cnoc àrsaidh in the north-west, the only good flint on Dia-thìr. Its grey flakes are carried to hearths from one end of the island to the other.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3500"><em>Murchadh goes out with the flint-carriers</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, GE 1,760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3502"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,790** — *Murchadh meets Ailig Spor on Rathad na Spor* (Cnoc àrsaidh). On the road between Cnoc àrsaidh and Cruinneachadh an Àtha, Murchadh comes to know Ailig Spor, a young carrier from the northern flats who tells him plainly that a yoke does not care whose back it is on; the two keep the friendship the whole of the years the road gives them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3501"><em>The lake still climbing on the Ros dhomhain rock</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, GE 1,760</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3503"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,800** — *Ailig marries by the northern crossing*. Ailig Spor marries a woman of a household by the river-crossing on Rathad na Spor and raises two sons and a daughter on flint-carrying wages, all three walking the near stretches of the road themselves before they are grown; Murchadh stands godfather to the eldest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3502"><em>Murchadh meets Ailig Spor on Rathad na Spor</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,790</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0130"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,817** — *The flint road* (Àth leathan). A track is worn by the flint-carriers from Cnoc àrsaidh south and east toward the ford gathering. Near Àth leathan their feet sink it a yard deep.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3504"><em>Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,817</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3504"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,817** — *Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep* (Cnoc àrsaidh). The track between Cnoc àrsaidh and the northern river-crossing, worn by generations of carriers before Murchadh and Ailig were born, sinks a full yard below the level of the ground on either side, so that a man walking it casts no shadow beyond its banks and a stranger cresting the rise above it mistakes it for a dry ditch dug on purpose.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0130"><em>The flint road</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,817</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3505"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,818** — *A storm survived in the sunken road's own bank* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Caught two days from shelter by a late storm, Ailig thinks to have the yoke-gang dig into the sunken road's bank and roof it with the carriers' own yokes rather than risk the open ground; the gang comes through with nothing worse than cold fingers, where an older carrier swears they would otherwise have lost two or three men.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3504"><em>Rathad na Spor worn a yard deep</em>, 11 am Faoilleach, GE 1,817</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3506"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, GE 1,820** — *The households along the road remark Murchadh's unaging face* (Cnoc àrsaidh). It does not escape the households of Rathad na Spor, decade upon decade, that Murchadh carries a yoke with no more sign of years on him than a carrier three seasons in shows; some later carriers will not share a fire with him for reasons they give badly, but Ailig never once asks him the plain question every other man on the circuit wants to ask.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3505"><em>A storm survived in the sunken road's own bank</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,818</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3507"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, GE 1,834** — *Ailig gives up the road for the pit-mouth* (Cnoc àrsaidh). In his sixty-fourth year Ailig Spor hands his yoke to his youngest son and takes the lighter work of tallying at the Cnoc àrsaidh pit-mouth; Murchadh, who could by then claim a dozen reasons to walk the far circuits instead, finds himself always coming back through Cnoc àrsaidh at the turn of a season to sit an evening with him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3506"><em>The households along the road remark Murchadh's unaging face</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, GE 1,820</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3508"></a>**3 am Faoilleach, GE 1,838** — *Ailig Spor dies* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Ailig Spor dies in his sleep in his sixty-eighth year, four years a keeper and not a carrier, found by his own daughter with no mark of pain on him; Murchadh, two days south with a fresh gang who scarcely know his name, walks the two days back in one and stands at the graveside with a stillness the household has not seen on him before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3507"><em>Ailig gives up the road for the pit-mouth</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, GE 1,834</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3509"></a>**1 an Gearran, GE 1,838** — *Murchadh sets the pit-mouth's free flake as a standing custom* (Cnoc àrsaidh). Murchadh stays at Cnoc àrsaidh the better part of a month after Ailig's burying and tells the new keeper that the pit's first flake of any new working shall go on being given free to whoever asks, as it always had, and that he will see to it himself that the custom does not lapse.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3508"><em>Ailig Spor dies</em>, 3 am Faoilleach, GE 1,838</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0131"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,853** — *The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr* (Àth mhòr). A hawk is carved on a lintel over a house door at Àth mhòr in the north, wings closed, head turned. It is the oldest carving of a hawk on the island, and of any bird.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3510"><em>The hawk carved into the lintel at Àth mhòr</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,853</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3510"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,853** — *The hawk carved into the lintel at Àth mhòr* (Àth mhòr). Walking the far eastern circuit alone, Murchadh watches a young man of Àth mhòr cut a hawk into his father's door-lintel by firelight over three evenings, wings closed and the head turned back over the shoulder; the carver says only that the shape came to him whole one night and would not leave him alone until he had cut it, and no carrier ever hears of an earlier bird cut in wood or stone anywhere on Dia-thìr.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0131"><em>The hawk lintel at Àth mhòr</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 1,853</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0132"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 1,890** — *Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich* (Tobar fhiadhaich). At Tobar fhiadhaich wolves are buried whole and with care, laid on their sides as people are. No other beast is so buried in this age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3511"><em>Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich</em>, 10 am Màrt, GE 1,890</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3511"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 1,890** — *Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich* (Tobar fhiadhaich). In his hundred and eighty-fifth year Murchadh comes upon a household at Tobar fhiadhaich burying a wolf on its side with its legs drawn up as in sleep; asked why, an old woman of the household says the wolf keeps its own dead on the high ground and has earned better than the ditch, a care they have never spoken of outside the household before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0132"><em>Wolves at Tobar fhiadhaich</em>, 10 am Màrt, GE 1,890</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3512"></a>**28 an Cèitean, GE 1,891** — *Murchadh asks his father for the north* (Dùn ìseal). Murchadh comes south to Dùn ìseal and asks his father for the whole northern country Rathad na Spor runs through, which he has walked, he says, more times than any man living and knows better than any man living knows it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3511"><em>Murchadh sees the wolves buried at Tobar fhiadhaich</em>, 10 am Màrt, GE 1,890</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3513"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,891** — *The king refuses Murchadh the north* (Dùn ìseal). The king answers that the north is Dòmhnall's to hold, given him sixteen hundred years before and well kept since, and that a share once given is not taken back for a better claim that comes after it; Murchadh rides north again within the week without asking a second time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3512"><em>Murchadh asks his father for the north</em>, 28 an Cèitean, GE 1,891</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3514"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,892** — *The first grievance of Ailean's line* (Dùn ìseal). Murchadh rides out of Dùn ìseal with a face his father's household has not seen on him before, nearer pride than the young man's face he wore going north the first time, and close under the pride, by the telling of those who marked it, the first grievance the hill ever had cause to lay at a son of Ailean's own naming.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3513"><em>The king refuses Murchadh the north</em>, 26 an t-Ògmhios, GE 1,891</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3515"></a>**23 an Lùnastal, GE 1,925** — *The high pastures fail at Dùn ìseal*. A spring of near-ceaseless rain rots the high grazing at the root, and households begin killing beasts they would ordinarily have wintered, for want of anything left to feed them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3028"><em>Sìleas born of the king's blood</em>, 9 am Màrt, GE 1,500</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3516"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, GE 1,926** — *Sìleas opens the store within the bank by the mouth, not the herd*. Sìleas Bhàn orders the grain-pits cut into Dùn ìseal's own earthwork opened to every household by the count of mouths at its hearth rather than by the size of its herd, the first time the store is shared by that measure; a wealthier herdsman rides up to protest it to her face, and she does not change the measure.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3515"><em>The high pastures fail at Dùn ìseal</em>, 23 an Lùnastal, GE 1,925</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0133"></a>**9 an Gearran, GE 1,927** — *Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years* (Dùn ìseal). Sìleas Bhàn, eighth of the Stone Kings, of the king's blood, holds Dùn ìseal through years of failed grazing. No deed is told of her but that she held, and the list goes on after her.
- <a id="ev-EII-3517"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, GE 1,928** — *Households begin refilling the store unasked*. With the grazing still short, households of Dùn ìseal's own ground begin returning grain to the bank's pits beyond what was drawn from them, a custom Sìleas Bhàn lets stand without ordering it, judging it will hold firmer for growing its own root.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0133"><em>Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 1,927</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3518"></a>**11 an Lùnastal, GE 1,929** — *The grazing recovers*. The high pastures dry and thicken again within three years of their failing, as such lean spells generally did on that ground, though the store within the bank is not filled to its old level again for a decade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3517"><em>Households begin refilling the store unasked</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, GE 1,928</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3519"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, GE 1,965** — *The hunger at Baile chrom is first heard of at the hill* (Baile chrom). Word reaches Dùn ìseal, slow and uncertain, of two failed fishing seasons on the north-western shore at Baile chrom, of stores already gone to bark and boiled seaweed, and of graves being laid two deep for want of time to dig them singly.
- <a id="ev-I-0134"></a>**7 an Cèitean, GE 1,966** — *The hunger at Baile chrom* (Gorta Baile chrom). Hunger comes to the settlement on the site of the north-western Baile chrom. Its pots are left full of boiled bark and seaweed, and its grave-rows are doubled. No older hunger on Dia-thìr is tied to a place.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3519"><em>The hunger at Baile chrom is first heard of at the hill</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, GE 1,965</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3520"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, GE 1,967** — *The king rides north-west with grain* (Baile chrom). Ailean Mòr rides to the north-western coast himself with the first grain that can be spared, by a road that has never before carried him, and is gone the better part of a season; he returns saying nothing of what he found, save that every hill of the kingdom is to look to its own store before the next storm season.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0134"><em>The hunger at Baile chrom</em>, 7 an Cèitean, GE 1,966</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3521"></a>**13 an Lùnastal, GE 1,967** — *Sìleas sends grain along the whole north-western coast* (Baile chrom). Sìleas Bhàn holds Dùn ìseal in the king's absence and sends three cartloads of grain and a small herd of goats after him, with instruction that they go to whichever hearths along that coast are worst served and not to Baile chrom alone, having heard the hunger reaches wider than one shore.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0134"><em>The hunger at Baile chrom</em>, 7 an Cèitean, GE 1,966</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3522"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, GE 1,968** — *No household near Dùn ìseal again lets its store run low*. Once the doubled grave-rows of Baile chrom are known at the hill, no household within a day's ride of Dùn ìseal again lets its own grain fall below a season's worth, whatever the grazing does, for fear of what might one day be asked of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0134"><em>The hunger at Baile chrom</em>, 7 an Cèitean, GE 1,966</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 2,001 – 2,250

- <a id="ev-EII-3523"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, GE 2,003** — *The wells of Achadh shean run low* (Achadh shean). The wells of Achadh shean in the east fall a hand lower than any digger there remembers, a thing thought at first too small to trouble the hill with.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3522"><em>No household near Dùn ìseal again lets its store run low</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, GE 1,968</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3524"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,004** — *A shepherd's boy walks to Dùn ìseal to report the cracking banks* (Achadh shean). A boy of Achadh shean walks three days to Dùn ìseal on his own feet rather than trust the telling to a rider, to say that the field banks his grandfather raised have cracked from dryness for the first time in three generations; Sìleas Bhàn sends a rider east to look before sending any grain.
- <a id="ev-EII-3525"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, GE 2,005** — *The springs of Achadh shean stop* (Achadh shean). The rider sent east returns saying the springs of Achadh shean have not merely run low but stopped outright, their whole visible flow gone at a season when they have never before failed within living telling.
- <a id="ev-I-0135"></a>**8 an Giblean, GE 2,006** — *The drought at Achadh shean* (Tiormachd Achadh shean). The springs of Achadh shean in the east run dry so long that the field banks are forsaken and grown over. When people return they cut new fields on another line.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3524"><em>A shepherd's boy walks to Dùn ìseal to report the cracking banks</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,004</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3525"><em>The springs of Achadh shean stop</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, GE 2,005</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-3526"><em>The field banks of Achadh shean are forsaken</em>, 8 an Giblean, GE 2,006</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3526"></a>**8 an Giblean, GE 2,006** — *The field banks of Achadh shean are forsaken* (Achadh shean). With the springs three years dry, the households of Achadh shean walk off their old field banks, leaving the dead barley standing in the row, and cut new fields on another line lower on the slope, where a lesser spring still runs thin but steady.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0135"><em>The drought at Achadh shean</em>, 8 an Giblean, GE 2,006</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3527"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, GE 2,007** — *Sìleas refuses to have the dead field pulled down* (Achadh shean). Riding out to see the forsaken banks of Achadh shean, Sìleas Bhàn refuses her own rider's suggestion that they be levelled, saying a bank tells a household what the ground once gave and what it stopped giving, and is worth more standing than pulled down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0135"><em>The drought at Achadh shean</em>, 8 an Giblean, GE 2,006</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3528"></a>**2 an Giblean, GE 2,008** — *Sìleas asks the king what her deed will be*. At Cruinneachadh an Àtha Sìleas Bhàn asks Ailean Mòr what the list will say she did, having herself set no boundary stone, fought no war and raided no shore; he tells her that four hundred years of not failing, where failing was always the easier road, is itself the deed the list will keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3527"><em>Sìleas refuses to have the dead field pulled down</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, GE 2,007</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3529"></a>**4 am Màrt, GE 2,010** — *Sìleas Bhàn gives Dùn ìseal to Tormod Liath*. In her five hundred and tenth year Sìleas Bhàn gives the hill to Tormod Liath, a son of Iain Dubh of thirteen hundred and seventy years, ordering the store within the bank counted before witnesses so the new holder takes it up knowing to the basket what it holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0133"><em>Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 1,927</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3530"></a>**14 am Màrt, GE 2,010** — *Tormod Liath keeps the grain-measure unchanged*. In his first words as holder, Tormod Liath tells the households he will change nothing about the store within the bank, having watched it feed two hungers in his own lifetime and seeing no reason to improve on a measure that has already held.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3529"><em>Sìleas Bhàn gives Dùn ìseal to Tormod Liath</em>, 4 am Màrt, GE 2,010</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3531"></a>**12 an Giblean, GE 2,021** — *Tormod mends the bank and the boundary marks* (Dùn ìseal). In his first seasons holding Dùn ìseal, Tormod Liath sets right what the hungry years let go: the silted ditch, the leaning palisade, and the boundary marks between the hill's fields and the households', blurred by two lean summers of each man taking what he could.
- <a id="ev-EII-3532"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, GE 2,040** — *Tormod buries his eldest son* (Dùn ìseal). Tormod Liath's eldest son dies of years, the first of the three heirs Tormod outlives; the old holder stands at the burying still dark-haired, and is named by his own son's grandchildren as their grandfather's father.
- <a id="ev-I-0136"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,047** — *The naming of the wind directions*. The eight winds are named, and every Dia-thìreach sailor after uses the names. Their meaning is dark even to those who speak them, and they have never been changed.
- <a id="ev-EII-3533"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, GE 2,047** — *Na h-Ochd Gaothan are named*. Na h-Ochd Gaothan of the year, known before only by their feel, are given names all at once by no one the coasts can afterward name. Every coast that tells it uses the same eight names in the same order from that year on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0136"><em>The naming of the wind directions</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,047</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3534"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, GE 2,048** — *Fearchar Gobha brings the wind-names to Tormod* (Dùn ìseal). A salt-carrier of the hill, Fearchar Gobha, hears the eight wind-names at the coast fair and brings them up to Tormod Liath, who says only that a landholder has no business owning what belongs to the sea.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0136"><em>The naming of the wind directions</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,047</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3535"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,050** — *Eilidh born in the valleys under the hill* (Dùn ìseal). A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under Dùn ìseal and named Eilidh; grey-eyed from her first year, she grows up at her own hearth with no thought of holding anything more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0136"><em>The naming of the wind directions</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,047</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3536"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, GE 2,076** — *Three brothers raise Clachan nan Gaoth at Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). Aonghas, Dùghlas and Ailig mac Torcaill, brothers of the point, quarry eight stones from an outcrop above the landing and raise them in a ring, one for each named wind, so a sailor may lay a hand on the stone of the wind he wants before he puts out.
- <a id="ev-I-0137"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,084** — *The wind-stones of Ceann leathan* (Ceann leathan). Eight tall stones are set in a ring on the point at Ceann leathan, one for each of the named winds. Sailors of every later age touch the stone of the wind they want before they put out.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3536"><em>Three brothers raise Clachan nan Gaoth at Ceann leathan</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, GE 2,076</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3537"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,084** — *The crooked stone reset* (Ceann leathan). One bad winter after Clachan nan Gaoth are first raised at Ceann leathan, the stone of the hardest offshore wind is found settled crooked and is dug out and reset on a footing of smaller stones, standing straighter and newer than its seven fellows ever after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0137"><em>The wind-stones of Ceann leathan</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,084</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3538"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,100** — *Tormod buries his second son on the western slope*. Tormod Liath's second son, who held the hill's western grazing and never cared for the hall, is buried at his own asking on the slope where he herded, and Tormod says a man ought to be let choose his own ground if nothing else is left him to choose.
- <a id="ev-I-0138"></a>**24 an Cèitean, GE 2,124** — *The wind-names carried to the islands* (Eilean fhada). The eight wind-names are used on Eilean fhada as on the main island. The markers on its high point bear eight cut notches, one facing each way.
- <a id="ev-EII-3539"></a>**30 an Cèitean, GE 2,124** — *The wind-names cut into the rock of Eilean fhada*. The people of Eilean fhada, off the northern cape, keep no ring of stones but cut the eight wind-names as notches into the rock of the island's highest ground, one facing each way, so a man lost in thick weather may find his bearing by touch.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0138"><em>The wind-names carried to the islands</em>, 24 an Cèitean, GE 2,124</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3540"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,160** — *Raghnall Ceannfhionn dies* (Dùn ìseal). Raghnall Ceannfhionn, who waded into the ford to strike the bargain of salt for wool, dies in his fourteen hundred and first year; the ford keeps its autumn meeting that year as every year, and the two hills send more wool and more salt than the bargain asks.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0113"><em>Raghnall Ceannfhionn makes peace</em>, 10 an Cèitean, GE 1,175</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0139"></a>**25 an Giblean, GE 2,163** — *Tormod Liath* (Dùn ìseal). Tormod Liath, ninth of the Stone Kings, a grandson of the king, holds the hill so long that he outlives three heirs, and is remembered as old. In his time Dùn ìseal is given its second bank, and its ground is doubled.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3531"><em>Tormod mends the bank and the boundary marks</em>, 12 an Giblean, GE 2,021</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3532"><em>Tormod buries his eldest son</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, GE 2,040</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3538"><em>Tormod buries his second son on the western slope</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,100</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3541"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,163** — *Tormod paces out the second bank* (Dùn ìseal). Tormod Liath walks the line of Dùn ìseal's second bank himself through two winters before calling the households in to dig, taking in the low ground by the spring without losing the height needed for a watch-fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3542"></a>**30 an Cèitean, GE 2,164** — *The households dig the second bank* (Dùn ìseal). The households of Dùn ìseal dig through a spring and a summer to raise the second bank, doubling the ground held within the hill's earth from some forty houses to very near a hundred.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3543"></a>**1 an Cèitean, GE 2,180** — *Tormod buries his third son and tells him it does not hurt* (Dùn ìseal). The youngest and last of Tormod Liath's three sons dies asking his father, near the end, whether it hurts to be left each time; Tormod tells him no, the one lie the tellings of that hill ever charge against him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3544"></a>**2 an Giblean, GE 2,185** — *Tormod goes fully grey* (Dùn ìseal). By his hundred and seventy-fifth year of holding, Tormod Liath is grey through, brows and beard with the rest, and the young of the hill, who never knew him dark, take him for the oldest thing on Dùn ìseal, older even than the second bank he raised.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3545"></a>**3 an Gearran, GE 2,193** — *The king raises Tormod from the mud at the gate* (Dùn ìseal). The king comes to Dùn ìseal's gate with a handful of his household and no word sent ahead; grey, stooped Tormod Liath kneels to him as every holder before him has knelt, and is raised again by a hand that has not aged since Tormod's father knelt the same way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3546"></a>**4 am Màrt, GE 2,193** — *A child asks why the old man kneels* (Dùn ìseal). A granddaughter of Tormod's second son, watching from the bank, asks her mother why the young stranger lets the old holder kneel to him as at a common gate; her mother tells her that evening, by the fire, what the hill has long known and rarely says aloud.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0139"><em>Tormod Liath</em>, 25 an Giblean, GE 2,163</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0140"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,201** — *The Dia-thìrich name*. In this age the hill-folk begin to call themselves Dia-thìrich and the island Dia-thìr. The first use is not known; the eldest tellings take both names for granted. With the names goes the belief: they did not come; they were here.
- <a id="ev-EII-3547"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, GE 2,201** — *Children begin to call themselves Dia-thìrich* (Dùn ìseal). The children of Dùn ìseal begin, unbidden by any elder, to call themselves Dia-thìrich and their island Dia-thìr, in place of hill-folk or the grove-born name Clann nan Dè; within a generation the old words fall out of use among the young.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0140"><em>The Dia-thìrich name</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,201</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3548"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, GE 2,201** — *Tormod is told the island's new name by a boy of seven* (Dùn ìseal). A boy of the new ground within the second bank tells Tormod Liath, asked what clan he is, that he is Dia-thìreach and that everyone is; Tormod answers only that it is a good enough name for a good enough island.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0140"><em>The Dia-thìrich name</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,201</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3549"></a>**15 an Gearran, GE 2,221** — *Ealag and Torcall Tochlair are promised by their households* (Dùn ìseal). Two households of the hill above Dùn ìseal, who share a slope and a spring, treat a match between Ealag and Torcall Tochlair as already settled. Torcall's mother carries the salt across to ask for it in the old way.
- <a id="ev-EII-3550"></a>**3 an Gearran, GE 2,222** — *The salt is refused* (Dùn ìseal). Torcall's mother brings the salt back unaccepted. The elders of Ealag's household give her no reason, only that the match cannot be, and she comes home with her face set as it had never been set before.
- <a id="ev-I-0141"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223** — *The first forbidden marriage*. A marriage between two lineages is forbidden, for a reason no surviving telling gives. Already the Dia-thìrich order themselves by blood, long before the coal gives them cause.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3549"><em>Ealag and Torcall Tochlair are promised by their households</em>, 15 an Gearran, GE 2,221</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3550"><em>The salt is refused</em>, 3 an Gearran, GE 2,222</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3551"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223** — *Torcall is turned away at every door* (Dùn ìseal). Torcall Tochlair goes himself to Ealag's father and her uncles and is told, in the same three words each time, that the marriage cannot be. None of them will say why, and he cannot tell whether none of them know it or all of them have sworn silence.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0141"><em>The first forbidden marriage</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3552"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, GE 2,223** — *Ealag's mother weeps and will not say* (Dùn ìseal). Ealag asks her own mother for the reason and is told only to stop asking, and her mother weeps, which Ealag has never seen her do, not even at a burying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0141"><em>The first forbidden marriage</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3553"></a>**1 an Cèitean, GE 2,224** — *Ealag given to a household of the ford* (Fèill Muileann òg). Ealag is married to Donnchadh, a fisher of the ford town, who asks for her honestly and does not learn of the earlier match for three years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0141"><em>The first forbidden marriage</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3554"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, GE 2,238** — *Torcall hears of the black hill in the east*. Torcall Tochlair, restless at the coal-banks under the mountain, hears from traders of ground in the east with a look of coal about it, and begins asking the older diggers whether the vein is the island's only one.
- <a id="ev-I-0142"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,247** — *Lines recited at the ford* (Fèill Muileann òg). At the ford gathering households begin to recite their lines aloud before any marriage is made, seven names back on either side. These are the first genealogies of the common households; only the Line of the Mason is older. None survives whole.
- <a id="ev-EII-3555"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, GE 2,247** — *The lines first recited at the ford*. Before any match is spoken at the fair, a household stands and gives its line aloud, seven names back on either side, so a forbidden blood may be named before the salt is carried. Ealag hears it and thinks of the four shut mouths that refused her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0142"><em>Lines recited at the ford</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,247</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3556"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,247** — *Ealag tells Donnchadh of Torcall* (Fèill Muileann òg). That evening Ealag tells her husband of the match that was refused her. He says only that it explains a look she sometimes wears at fair-time, and asks nothing further.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-I-0142"><em>Lines recited at the ford</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,247</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3557"></a>**5 am Faoilleach, GE 2,250** — *Calum born to Eilidh* (Dùn ìseal). A son is born to Eilidh in the valleys under the hill and named Calum, dark from his birth; he will be the elder of her two sons and the one who stands where an heir stands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0142"><em>Lines recited at the ford</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,247</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 2,251 – 2,500

- <a id="ev-EII-3558"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, GE 2,262** — *Lachann agrees to go east with his brother* (Cnoc na Claise). Torcall's younger brother Lachann, easier in temper but loyal to him, agrees to go east to the black hill with two other restless diggers, meaning to see Torcall satisfied and brought home again.
- <a id="ev-I-0143"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,267** — *The first seeking of another vein* (Cnoc dhubh). Diggers from Dùn ìseal open a trench on a hill near Cnoc dhubh in the east, seeking coal like the vein's. They leave it unfinished when two of them are crushed by a fall. The trench stays open, and what it would have found is not known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3554"><em>Torcall hears of the black hill in the east</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, GE 2,238</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3558"><em>Lachann agrees to go east with his brother</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, GE 2,262</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3559"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,267** — *Lachann buried at the trench's mouth* (Cnoc na Claise). Torcall will not have his brother carried elsewhere and buries him where he fell, at the mouth of the trench on the black hill. The other man killed with him is carried home by his own people.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0143"><em>The first seeking of another vein</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,267</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3560"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, GE 2,268** — *Torcall builds a shelter at the trench* (Cnoc na Claise). When the other diggers pack their tools and go back to the coal-banks under the mountain, Torcall Tochlair stays, and builds himself a turf shelter at the trench's edge for the winter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0143"><em>The first seeking of another vein</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,267</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3561"></a>**12 an Lùnastal, GE 2,270** — *Word of Torcall reaches Ealag* (Fèill Muileann òg). A trader who stopped at the black hill brings word to the ford of a man sitting alone beside an open trench with his brother in the ground nearby, still saying he means to find the coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0143"><em>The first seeking of another vein</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,267</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0144"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 2,289** — *The stone that would not break*. A second opening for a new vein is made elsewhere on the island and fails wholly: common rock, and nothing beneath it. So it is first known that the vein under the mountain is alone of its kind.
- <a id="ev-EII-3562"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, GE 2,290** — *The saying of the vein's choosing begins to travel*. After the second opening strikes only unbroken common stone, it is said across the island that the vein under the mountain is alone of its kind and chose its one place the way na Seachd Guail are said to have chosen theirs.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0144"><em>The stone that would not break</em>, 10 am Màrt, GE 2,289</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3563"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, GE 2,300** — *Ealag dies at the ford* (Fèill Muileann òg). Ealag dies in her own bed at the ford with her children about her, having lived her whole life after the refusal without the reason for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0141"><em>The first forbidden marriage</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,223</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3564"></a>**17 an Cèitean, GE 2,305** — *The will for a third opening goes out of the island*. No elder forbids a third trench outright, but the wish for one fades everywhere at once, the way the wish for a refused match fades in two households without a word spoken between them.
- <a id="ev-EII-3565"></a>**18 an Giblean, GE 2,310** — *A household gathers at the black hill's foot* (Cnoc na Claise). Folk who come to the black hill for one reason or another begin to stay, since the ground is as good as any and the man who keeps the open trench asks nothing of them.
- <a id="ev-I-0145"></a>**8 an Giblean, GE 2,312** — *The prospecting ends*. No one tries a third opening in this age. The Dia-thìrich hold that the vein chooses where it lies, and that the choice is not theirs to try.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-3564"><em>The will for a third opening goes out of the island</em>, 17 an Cèitean, GE 2,305</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EII-3565"><em>A household gathers at the black hill's foot</em>, 18 an Giblean, GE 2,310</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-3566"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,318** — *Torcall Tochlair dies at the trench* (Cnoc na Claise). Torcall Tochlair dies at the black hill and is buried beside his brother at the trench's mouth. The household he gathered keeps the ground and does not fill the trench in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0143"><em>The first seeking of another vein</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,267</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0146"></a>**7 an Cèitean, GE 2,328** — *The first shared meal law*. A custom arises, unwritten, that any household with food to spare shall share it before the storm season.
- <a id="ev-EII-4000"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, GE 2,331** — *The shore-woman's catch carried in whole* (Dùn ìseal). A woman of the shore households at Dùn ìseal, whose net takes more mackerel than her family can eat or smoke before it turns, carries three baskets of it to the bank herself rather than let it spoil unshared. Tormod Liath comes down from the hall to help her set them down. After it the sharing before the storms needs no one to ask.
- <a id="ev-EII-4001"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 2,340** — *A holder shamed into doubling his own surplus* (Dùn ìseal). A holder of one of the near valleys mocks a household that brings little to the sharing. His neighbours say nothing against him, but the next year he brings in double his own surplus unasked. No reciter keeps his name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0146"><em>The first shared meal law</em>, 7 an Cèitean, GE 2,328</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0147"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,356** — *Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). At Dùn ìseal the sharing before the storms is done in the open: every household brings its surplus within the bank, and it is divided by the count of mouths. The custom has no earlier place that is known.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4000"><em>The shore-woman's catch carried in whole</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, GE 2,331</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4002"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 2,360** — *Beasag born at Àth shean* (Àth shean). A daughter is born to a careful household at Àth shean, the ford below Dùn ìseal, some years after her father digs a grain pit under the byre floor against nothing he can name. Her mother dies bearing the last of her brothers three winters before the lean year that will end the household's place at the ford.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4001"><em>A holder shamed into doubling his own surplus</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, GE 2,340</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4003"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, GE 2,360** — *Lachlann born on An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). A son is born in An Cnoc Ruadh's hall and named Lachlann, red-headed like so many of that line; he grows up wet to the knee on the lake shore and learns the salt-rake before the spear.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-3557"><em>Calum born to Eilidh</em>, 5 am Faoilleach, GE 2,250</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4004"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,370** — *Oighrig born to a herder of the near slopes* (Tobar dhìreach). A daughter is born to Dòmhnall, a herder of the near slopes above Tobar dhìreach with no kinship to Rìghrean na Cloiche, and named Oighrig; she grows up sitting her household's turns at the slab and will draw the white stone at three-and-thirty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0147"><em>Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,356</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4005"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 2,377** — *A lean storm season at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Failed grazing and short-headed barley along the near valleys, with three weeks lost to a wind that will not turn, make the leanest storm season since the sharing began. The division at the bank is thinner than any household remembers, and old people come to be counted though they have nothing to bring.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0147"><em>Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,356</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4006"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,377** — *Beasag watches the division made by the count of mouths* (Dùn ìseal). Beasag, seventeen, is sent to Dùn ìseal with her household's share in the lean year and sees the sharing divided by the count of mouths: a widow with four children carries home more than she brought, and a boy holds his first full sack too long to trust it. She says nothing of her father's pit.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0147"><em>Surplus shared at Dùn ìseal</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,356</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0148"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378** — *A household turned out at Àth shean* (Àth shean). A household at Àth shean hides its spare grain in a pit under the floor and brings nothing to the sharing. When the pit is found the household is put out of the settlement with what it can carry. It is the first punishment under the custom that is remembered.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4007"><em>Beasag tells of her father's pit at the ford</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4008"><em>Tormod Liath sends to open the floor at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4009"><em>The household of Àth shean put out with what it can carry</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4007"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378** — *Beasag tells of her father's pit at the ford* (Àth shean). In the first mild days after the storms break, a woman mending net on the bank at Àth shean asks Beasag idly whether her father's byre came through the lean year as thin as the rest. Beasag answers true: there is a pit under the floor, and he never brought it all in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0148"><em>A household turned out at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4008"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378** — *Tormod Liath sends to open the floor at Àth shean* (Dùn ìseal). Word of the hidden pit reaches Tormod Liath at Dùn ìseal by way of Àth shean's own holder. He asks only whether the girl told it of her own will, unbeaten and unbribed, and on being told she had, sends his men to open the floor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0148"><em>A household turned out at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4009"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378** — *The household of Àth shean put out with what it can carry* (Àth shean). Grain enough for two households through the lean winter is found beneath the byre floor. Beasag's father is given until dark to take what his household can carry on its backs and to be off the ford's ground by morning: the first punishment under the sharing custom that is remembered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0148"><em>A household turned out at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4010"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 2,379** — *Beasag's household settles east of the vein*. After eleven days on the road, Beasag's father builds a house on a nameless slope east of the vein, where the king's blood holds no hall and claims no grazing, among households that went out a generation before for their own reasons. He digs no pit under this floor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0148"><em>A household turned out at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4011"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,380** — *Sìleas Bhàn dies among her kin* (Dùn ìseal). Sìleas Bhàn, who opened the store within the bank by the count of mouths, dies among her own kin in the valley below the bank in her eight hundred and eightieth year; Tormod Liath comes down from the hall to stand at her burying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0133"><em>Sìleas Bhàn and the hungry years</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 1,927</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4012"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,385** — *Peigi born on An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). A daughter is born to Lachlann Ruadh and named Peigi, black-haired and loud from her first night; she will meet her father's fosterling at the gate at fifteen and tell him he is too thin.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4003"><em>Lachlann born on An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 5 an t-Sultain, GE 2,360</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4013"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, GE 2,390** — *Tormod Liath dies at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Tormod Liath dies in his own hall, without wound or fever, in the three hundred and eightieth year of his holding, having outlived three heirs of his own body and buried each at the bank he built. Dùn ìseal mourns him the length of a season; scarcely a household on the hill remembers a holder before him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4010"><em>Beasag's household settles east of the vein</em>, 12 an Cèitean, GE 2,379</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4014"></a>**14 an Gearran, GE 2,390** — *Eilidh Ghlas takes up the hill* (Dùn ìseal). The holding of Dùn ìseal passes to Eilidh Ghlas, of the king's own blood, who has lived out those same generations in the valleys under the hill without thought of holding anything but her own hearth. She takes up the sharing custom with the hill itself, and weighs it at the bank herself in her first years.
- <a id="ev-EII-4015"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 2,390** — *Eilidh Ghlas asks after the pit at Àth shean* (Àth shean). Before the bank is even swept for the season's grain, Eilidh Ghlas sends to Àth shean to ask after the pit still known by the name of the man who dug it. She is told it stands empty, and says only that this is well.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0148"><em>A household turned out at Àth shean</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 2,378</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4016"></a>**15 am Màrt, GE 2,391** — *Calum Ciar stands where an heir stands* (Dùn ìseal). In the first sharing of his mother's own holding, Calum Ciar stands a pace behind Eilidh Ghlas's shoulder at the bank, and the ford takes notice of him for the first time. No one at Dùn ìseal afterward looks for another heir.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4012"><em>Peigi born on An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,385</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4017"></a>**13 an Giblean, GE 2,393** — *Eilidh weighs the old custom of the valleys* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh Ghlas turns over, without acting on it, a custom she learned as a girl in the near valleys: that a household with two sons sometimes sends the younger to be raised at another hearth, so that he grows up loved rather than waiting on an inheritance not his.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4016"><em>Calum Ciar stands where an heir stands</em>, 15 am Màrt, GE 2,391</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4018"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,394** — *The younger son born in a high river spring* (Dùn ìseal). A second son is born to Eilidh Ghlas at Dùn ìseal in a wet spring, when the river at Àth shean runs high enough to float the ford-stones. No reciter keeps his day, and none ever will.
- <a id="ev-I-0149"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Eilidh Ghlas* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh Ghlas, tenth of the Stone Kings, of the king's blood, sends her younger son to the Red Hill to be fostered, the first fostering in either list. The son's name is not kept; only that he went, and that the peace of the ford held while he was there.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4014"><em>Eilidh Ghlas takes up the hill</em>, 14 an Gearran, GE 2,390</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4018"><em>The younger son born in a high river spring</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,394</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4019"><em>A boy who does not ask to ride out</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4020"><em>Word sent west to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4021"><em>Calum Ciar counts the miles at the gate</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4022"><em>Eilidh's parting at Àth shean</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4019"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *A boy who does not ask to ride out* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh's younger son, six years old, watches his brother ride out with the men to renew the boundary stones and does not ask to go. His mother watches him a long while from the hall door and tells her steward that a house with only one door out of it is no house for a second son.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0149"><em>Eilidh Ghlas</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4020"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Word sent west to An Cnoc Ruadh* (Dùn ìseal). Eilidh Ghlas sends word to Lachlann Ruadh, holder of An Cnoc Ruadh, asking that he take her younger son to be raised in his household. She gives it out as a mother's wish that the boy learn a trade of his own; the ford's peace is served by it besides.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0149"><em>Eilidh Ghlas</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4021"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Calum Ciar counts the miles at the gate* (Dùn ìseal). On the morning his brother leaves for An Cnoc Ruadh, Calum Ciar stands long at the gate after the party is out of sight, and tells a groom who asks him in out of the wind that he is only counting how many days fifty miles there and back will take.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0149"><em>Eilidh Ghlas</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4022"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Eilidh's parting at Àth shean* (Àth shean). Eilidh Ghlas walks with her son's party as far as Àth shean and kneels to his height at the turning of the roads, telling him he is not sent for any wrong of his, that An Cnoc Ruadh will be as much home to him as Dùn ìseal, and that she means to see him grown.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0149"><em>Eilidh Ghlas</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4023"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *A mound left untouched on Rathad an t-Salainn*. On the road west, the household man Donnchadh stops before a low green mound and will go no nearer to it, telling the boy only that it is older than the road and the salt trade. A wise traveller, he is told, lets such places lie as he lets a wasp's nest lie.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4022"><em>Eilidh's parting at Àth shean</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4024"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Rìonach's saying of the forked river* (Àth shean). Turning off Rathad an t-Salainn for her own kin at Àth shean, Rìonach tells the fosterling that a household not his own by birth is no loss to him but a doubling, as a forked river becomes two whole rivers rather than two lesser ones.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4023"><em>A mound left untouched on Rathad an t-Salainn</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4025"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *The fosterling comes to An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). Eilidh Ghlas's younger son comes down to the western lake shore at evening and is met at the gate by Lachlann Ruadh and his daughter Peigi, who tells her father plainly that he is too thin and will need feeding, and carries in his one bundle herself.
- <a id="ev-EII-4026"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400** — *Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son* (Cathair dhearg). Lachlann Ruadh tells his household that the fosterling shall be called no king's son and no king's grandson, but a boy of the ford's people come to learn a trade, and warns his daughter Peigi he will hear of it if she names him otherwise again.
- <a id="ev-I-0150"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,401** — *Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling* (Cathair dhearg). Lachlann Ruadh, holder of the Red Hill, takes the son of Eilidh Ghlas into his house. For it he is named Lachlann an Altraim, 'Lachlann of the fostering', and the Red Hill list calls him so more often than by his own name.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4025"><em>The fosterling comes to An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4026"><em>Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4027"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,401** — *Calum Ciar given the boundary stones* (Dùn ìseal). Calum Ciar is given the judging of the near valleys' boundary stones, the first trust of its kind laid on him, and settles a dispute between two herders over a shifted marker with a plainness his mother is said to have approved of.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4026"><em>Lachlann forbids the naming of a king's son</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4028"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,401** — *The fosterling first put out on the lake* (Cathair dhearg). The fosterling is let out on Loch chrom in a boat for the first time, and comes back to An Cnoc Ruadh wet through and pleased with himself, word of it carried east along Rathad an t-Salainn to Dùn ìseal by the carriers who walk it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4027"><em>Calum Ciar given the boundary stones</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,401</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4029"></a>**31 am Màrt, GE 2,402** — *Eilidh Ghlas visits An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). Eilidh Ghlas comes to An Cnoc Ruadh as Lachlann Ruadh's guest and sits at his own board four days, asking after the tallies and the weather as she asks after her son. Walking with her son to the western point of the lake, she tells him she will not come again for some years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0149"><em>Eilidh Ghlas</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,400</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4030"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, GE 2,402** — *The fosterling rakes salt without breaking the crust* (Cathair dhearg). Lachlann Ruadh puts a salt-rake into the fosterling's hands on the drying platform above Loch chrom and shows him the turn of the wrist his own family has kept for generations. By the fourth stroke the boy lifts a clean sheet of crust whole, and Peigi Dhubh tells him it is better than she managed her own first year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4029"><em>Eilidh Ghlas visits An Cnoc Ruadh</em>, 31 am Màrt, GE 2,402</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4031"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,402** — *An Cnoc Ruadh list begins to call Lachlann of the fostering* (Cathair dhearg). In these years An Cnoc Ruadh's reciters take up the habit of naming Lachlann Ruadh also Lachlann an Altraim, Lachlann of the fostering, until in time the second name is given by the list where the first once stood, and is never afterward unsaid.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0150"><em>Lachlann Ruadh takes the fosterling</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,401</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4032"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, GE 2,403** — *Beathag gives up the list of the slab's turns* (Tobar dhìreach). Beathag, who has kept the household order of the slab's night watch eleven years, says at the Samhain gathering that she will keep the list no longer, after a household comes two nights running to a turn already missed. Thirty-one households now stand on it, too many for one memory to hold true.
- <a id="ev-EII-4033"></a>**30 am Màrt, GE 2,403** — *The families agree to choose the slab's keeper by lot* (Tobar dhìreach). At the slab's own clearing the families of Tobar dhìreach and the near valleys meet to settle the watch. An old man of the gathering proposes a single keeper chosen by lot, to hold the slab until death or infirmity, rather than turns by household. No vote is taken; the silence that follows is read as agreement.
- <a id="ev-I-0151"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403** — *Oighrig, first keeper by lot* (Tobar dhìreach). The families who watch the slab agree to choose one keeper at a time by lot, and no longer to take turns by household. The first lot falls to a woman called Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill, and she keeps the slab for the rest of her life.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4032"><em>Beathag gives up the list of the slab's turns</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, GE 2,403</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4033"><em>The families agree to choose the slab's keeper by lot</em>, 30 am Màrt, GE 2,403</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4034"><em>The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4034"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403** — *The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill* (Tobar dhìreach). At the next full dark, thirty-one households send one member each to draw from a bag of thirty pebbles and one marked white. The lot falls to Oighrig, a herder's daughter of three-and-thirty, who carries the marked stone in her belt from that night for the rest of her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0151"><em>Oighrig, first keeper by lot</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4035"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,403** — *Oighrig's father speaks of the shared name* (Tobar dhìreach). Walking home from the drawing, Oighrig's father Dòmhnall, a herder of the near slopes with no kinship to Rìghrean na Cloiche, tells her she will spend the rest of her keeping answering travellers who mistake her for blood of Dòmhnall Clachach, the second of that name to hold the north.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4034"><em>The lot falls to Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0152"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, GE 2,404** — *The keepers' house* (Tobar dhìreach). A house is built beside the slab at Tobar dhìreach for the holder of the lot, its door facing the stone. It is rebuilt on the same footing many times. It is the first building on Dia-thìr made only to be near the vein.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4036"><em>Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, GE 2,404</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4036"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, GE 2,404** — *Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach* (Tobar dhìreach). The families of the near valleys build Oighrig a house on the clearing's edge above the slab, its door set to face the stone and no other way, the first building on Dia-thìr raised for no reason but to stand near the vein.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0152"><em>The keepers' house</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, GE 2,404</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4037"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,404** — *Oighrig sits her first winter alone by the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). Moved into the new house at the first hard frost, Oighrig finds the keeper's long unbroken watch harder than any turn shared with her own household, and begins to notice things about the stain and the stone's temper that a thousand years of turned watches had never set down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-4036"><em>Taigh na Lice raised at Tobar dhìreach</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, GE 2,404</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0153"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405** — *The stone cup* (Tobar dhìreach). Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill has a cup ground out of grey stone to the size of her own cupped hand, that the handful of coal may be the same for every household. The cup is carried round the hill settlements. Whether it outlasts the age is not known.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4038"><em>Oighrig comes to Niocol Snaidhear with her cupped hand</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4039"><em>The first two stone cups crack in the grinding</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4038"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405** — *Oighrig comes to Niocol Snaidhear with her cupped hand* (Tobar dhìreach). In her third year of keeping, Oighrig goes to the stone-worker Niocol Snaidhear and sets her own hand on his bench, cupped as for water, asking for a cup of grey stone that will hold exactly what it holds, so that no household's handful of coal runs bigger than another's by the accident of whose palm measures it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0153"><em>The stone cup</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4039"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405** — *The first two stone cups crack in the grinding* (Tobar dhìreach). Niocol Snaidhear loses a first cup to a hidden vein in the stone and a second to a hair-crack struck too hard near its finishing, and keeps the flawed second on his bench through the grinding of the third as a thing to learn the shape of a mistake by.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0153"><em>The stone cup</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4040"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, GE 2,406** — *Niocol finishes the cup ground to Oighrig's hand* (Tobar dhìreach). After eleven sittings across two summers, Niocol Snaidhear finishes a cup of grey stone fitted to Oighrig's hand, veined faintly white, holding exactly what her two cupped hands together cannot quite hold. She says the hand it copies is not her own but the hand of every hearth; Niocol begins a second cup as a copy before he is asked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0153"><em>The stone cup</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, GE 2,405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4041"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,406** — *Word of the stone cup travels the near valleys* (Àth gharbh). News of Oighrig's cup and the trouble it answers reaches stone-workers at three other places within the year: a woman at Àth gharbh, an old man at Achadh dhìreach, and a household at Cnoc chaol, each asking to grind a copy against it.
- <a id="ev-I-0154"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407** — *The stone cup copied* (Cnoc chaol). Copies of the keeper's cup are ground at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol, each tried against the first by filling it with water. Thereafter the hill settlements measure the coal with one measure.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4041"><em>Word of the stone cup travels the near valleys</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,406</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4042"><em>Oighrig carries the first cup to Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4043"><em>The four cups are ground true at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4042"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407** — *Oighrig carries the first cup to Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol* (Àth gharbh). Oighrig walks the near valleys over a year with the first cup wrapped in wool, testing each new copy against it by pouring water from one to the other on a flat stone, and sending two cups at Achadh dhìreach and one at Cnoc chaol back to the wheel when the levels do not match.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0154"><em>The stone cup copied</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4043"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407** — *The four cups are ground true at Àth gharbh, Achadh dhìreach and Cnoc chaol* (Àth gharbh). The copies of the stone cup are finished: quickest at Àth gharbh, where the worker measures against Niocol's cup throughout rather than a hand alone; slowest at Achadh dhìreach, an old man's hands steadied by his grandson through the last evenings; and, despite two false starts, fastest of all begun at Cnoc chaol.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0154"><em>The stone cup copied</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, GE 2,407</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0154a"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408** — *The meeting of the cups* (Coinneachadh nan Cupan). The keeper's cup and its three copies are carried to a spring on the moor between Àth gharbh and Tobar dhìreach, set side by side on a flat stone and filled from the spring in turn. The place is called Coinneachadh nan Cupan, the meeting of the cups. The hill settlements return to it whenever a cup is broken and a new one must be tried.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4044"><em>Coinneachadh nan Cupan on the moor</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4045"><em>The hills measure the coal with one measure</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4044"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408** — *Coinneachadh nan Cupan on the moor*. At a nameless spring on the moor between Àth gharbh and Tobar dhìreach, chosen because it lies equal walking from all four places and belongs to no one household, the four keepers of the cups fill each from the same water on a flat stone and pass every cup down the line for each hand to weigh. The water stands level in all four; the place is called from that morning Coinneachadh nan Cupan.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0154a"><em>The meeting of the cups</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4045"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408** — *The hills measure the coal with one measure* (Tobar dhìreach). From the year of Coinneachadh nan Cupan, the households from the slopes above Tobar dhìreach to the poor ground of Cnoc chaol measure their handful of the vein's coal by the one cup and its three copies, and not by the hand that happens to do the measuring, a change the reciters afterward give no more than a single line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0154a"><em>The meeting of the cups</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4046"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 2,408** — *Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill dies keeping the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). Oighrig nic Dhòmhnaill keeps the slab for the rest of her life, as the lot gave it her, and that rest is shorter than anyone at the clearing looked for: she dies in Taigh na Lice in the winter after Coinneachadh nan Cupan, and the families ask that a new lot be drawn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0151"><em>Oighrig, first keeper by lot</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0155"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409** — *Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal* (Eilean chrom). A keeper by lot, Gilleasbuig Beag, is found with a basket of broken coal from the vein in his own house. The households of the hills sit in judgement at the slab, row him out to Eilean chrom, and leave him there without a boat. He is the first known to be exiled for the vein.
- <a id="ev-EII-4047"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409** — *The lot falls to Gilleasbuig Beag* (Tobar dhìreach). The bag of pebbles is filled again and passed among the households near the crack. The white stone comes out in the hand of Gilleasbuig Beag, a broad, quiet man known for mending roofs and cutting hazel, who goes pale rather than glad at what his open hand shows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0151"><em>Oighrig, first keeper by lot</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4048"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, GE 2,409** — *A basket found under the bed-place* (Tobar dhìreach). A kinswoman of Gilleasbuig, in his house on another errand, lifts a cloth expecting food and finds a basket of broken coal from the vein, more than any hand is owed by the handful. She says nothing that day, but tells her husband before she sleeps, and within three days the near valley knows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4049"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, GE 2,409** — *Gilleasbuig does not deny it* (Tobar dhìreach). Called to the clearing, Gilleasbuig Beag owns the basket at once and says he took the coal against a hard winter, for an old mother who sleeps cold, and for no other use. He asks, when the judgement is given, what the stone gains by the coal's return that his mother does not lose by going without it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4050"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, GE 2,409** — *The families judge Gilleasbuig by silence* (Tobar dhìreach). The households argue long in the cold before an old woman of Cnoc chaol says what none of the near families will say first: that the vein was never any one hearth's to keep behind a cloth, however true the love that took it. The clearing's silence, held past any voice rising to answer it, stands as the judgement.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4051"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, GE 2,409** — *Gilleasbuig Beag rowed to Eilean chrom*. Three men of the near households row Gilleasbuig Beag out to Eilean chrom and put him ashore, then pull back to open water and leave him without a boat to return in. He is the first anyone remembers exiled for the vein.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4052"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, GE 2,409** — *A fire seen three nights on Eilean chrom*. The near coast watches a small fire on Eilean chrom's low rise the first night, smaller the second, and a coal's worth of red at dusk the third, gone before full dark. No fire is seen there again, and no boat is sent to learn why.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4053"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, GE 2,409** — *The basket set inside Taigh na Lice* (Tobar dhìreach). The kinswoman who found the coal carries the basket to Taigh na Lice at Tobar dhìreach and sets it under its cloth just inside the door. No household proposes burning it; it was not theirs to burn before Gilleasbuig took it, and the judgement has settled that it never will be.
- <a id="ev-EII-4054"></a>**21 an t-Samhain, GE 2,409** — *The lot falls to Giorsal Bhàn* (Tobar dhìreach). A new lot is drawn from the same bag that gave the stone to Oighrig and then to Gilleasbuig, and this time it is Giorsal Bhàn's hand that opens on the white pebble. She closes her hand on it and says she will keep it, and moves into Taigh na Lice before the month is out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0151"><em>Oighrig, first keeper by lot</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 2,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0156"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411** — *The coal returned to the crack* (Tobar dhìreach). The coal from Gilleasbuig Beag's house is neither burned nor kept. The keeper after him carries it back to the slab and lays it beneath, piece by piece. The tellings make much of it: the coal went home.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4053"><em>The basket set inside Taigh na Lice</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, GE 2,409</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4055"><em>Giorsal lays the coal back under the slab</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4056"><em>"The coal went home"</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4055"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411** — *Giorsal lays the coal back under the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). On a still morning near the year's turn, Giorsal Bhàn kneels at the slab's lower edge and presses the broken coal back into the gap between stone and earth, piece by piece, returning a second day to finish it, until the basket holds nothing at all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0156"><em>The coal returned to the crack</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4056"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411** — *"The coal went home"* (Tobar dhìreach). By the summer after Giorsal Bhàn empties the basket into the slab's edge, the four words are already going round the near valley as if they had always been there: that the coal went home. No one near the crack can afterward say who spoke them first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0156"><em>The coal returned to the crack</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,411</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4057"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, GE 2,411** — *Eilean chrom left to itself*. The island stands ungrazed and unfished through the years after Gilleasbuig Beag's exile. Children of the near coast are told not to ask about the island with the spring on it, and are given the same short answer when they ask anyway.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0155"><em>Gilleasbuig Beag takes coal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, GE 2,409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0157"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412** — *Calum Ciar asks for the lot* (Dùn ìseal). Calum Ciar, the elder son of Eilidh Ghlas and eleventh of the Stone Kings, asks that the keeper's lot be drawn at Dùn ìseal in his sight. The households at the slab refuse him. The list sets down the refusal, which is more than it sets down of most things.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4058"><em>Calum Ciar comes to the clearing</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4059"><em>The families refuse Calum Ciar</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4058"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412** — *Calum Ciar comes to the clearing* (Tobar dhìreach). Calum Ciar, elder son of Eilidh Ghlas and eleventh to hold Dùn ìseal under the king, walks up the valley to the slab and asks that the next lot be drawn at Dùn ìseal in his own sight, so the hill may see the vein's lot drawn as honestly as the hill's own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0157"><em>Calum Ciar asks for the lot</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4059"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412** — *The families refuse Calum Ciar* (Tobar dhìreach). The households near the crack answer Calum Ciar with the same held silence they gave Gilleasbuig Beag: the lot has been drawn at the slab since the custom began and will go on being drawn there, in the sight of whoever near the crack cares to watch. Calum Ciar thanks them and does not argue it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0157"><em>Calum Ciar asks for the lot</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, GE 2,412</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4060"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, GE 2,413** — *Calum Ciar puts the question to the king*. At the ford that summer, Calum Ciar carries the same question to the king. The king hears him without anger or haste and says only that the slab is older than the hill, and older than the grove of his own crowning, and that he will not overrule so old a thing for the asking of a man not two hundred years in the world.
- <a id="ev-I-0158"></a>**7 an Cèitean, GE 2,416** — *The kings and the keepers* (Dùn ìseal). After the refusal of Calum Ciar the lot is still drawn at the slab. The holders of the hill rule the grazing and the gatherings under the king, but not the vein, and the king does not overrule the slab. The line between the two holds for the rest of the age. It is not yet written anywhere.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-4060"><em>Calum Ciar puts the question to the king</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, GE 2,413</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-4061"><em>The line between hill and slab holds unwritten</em>, 7 an Cèitean, GE 2,416</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-4061"></a>**7 an Cèitean, GE 2,416** — *The line between hill and slab holds unwritten* (Dùn ìseal). Calum Ciar goes home from the ford and asks nothing more of it. The hill rules the grazing and calls the gatherings, answering to the king for both; the keepers rule the vein, answering to no one the telling can name.
