- <a id="ev-EII-5519"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,022** — *Beathan's son clears the path for Somhairle's stick* (Tobar dhìreach). In Somhairle's last seasons, Beathan's son walks up before each Samhain to clear fallen branches from the path so the old man's stick will not catch in the dark, and sits longer at the slab on the nights Somhairle climbs to it, though no household asks this of him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5518"><em>Somhairle asks Diorbhail what waits for a man with no hall</em>, 20 an Cèitean, GE 3,018</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0104a"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025** — *Somhairle mac Ailein dies* (Tobar dhìreach). Somhairle mac Ailein, a son of Ailean Mòr born in his father's sixty-second year, dies in the high valleys at two thousand nine hundred and eighty-seven years, before his father. His line lives among Clann na Ceiste and holds no share of the hill. In each generation after him the long years are shorter.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5057"><em>Diorbhail says her own line before she can tie a shoe</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, GE 2,993</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5058"><em>Somhairle first sits Diorbhail by the slab</em>, 4 an Cèitean, GE 2,997</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5515"><em>Somhairle gives Diorbhail Sloinneadh a' Chlachair whole</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,010</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-5520"><em>Beathan's son finds Somhairle dead against the slab</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-5521"><em>The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5520"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025** — *Beathan's son finds Somhairle dead against the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). In the season the valleys keep for turning peat, Beathan's son finds Somhairle sitting against the slab in the grey of a morning, his stick fallen just out of reach, with no mark on him anywhere; word goes down to Dùn ìseal before noon on the fastest pony the round can put under a boy.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104a"><em>Somhairle mac Ailein dies</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5521"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025** — *The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil* (Tobar dhìreach). The king comes up on foot the last two miles, buries his son with his own two hands beside the slab, and sits on the turf afterward with his arms round his knees until an old reciter comes to ask, well after dark, whether he will come in to the fire.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104a"><em>Somhairle mac Ailein dies</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5522"></a>**20 an Cèitean, GE 3,026** — *Beathan's son takes up the whole watch at the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). With no household troubling to make it formal, Beathan's son takes the watch at the slab as his own to keep entire, as his father had kept it before Somhairle first divided the watching from the reciting between two hands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5521"><em>The king buries Somhairle and keeps a night's vigil</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0209"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,028** — *Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore* (Ceann mhin). The south-eastern Ceann mhin is settled near Làrach an Dùin. Its people are the first to live in sight of the fortress ruin, and they will not go up to it.
- <a id="ev-EII-5523"></a>**21 an Giblean, GE 3,030** — *Diorbhail keeps the Line by mouth and takes no share for it* (Tobar dhìreach). Diorbhail says the whole Line through twice each Samhain to any of the watch-households who will hear it, adding each year's names to its foot and setting none of it down on leaf or hide, and takes no share from any hall for the keeping, as Somhairle held she must.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0104a"><em>Somhairle mac Ailein dies</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,025</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5524"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, GE 3,040** — *Ceann mhin's people will not climb to the ruin* (Ceann mhin). The households settled in sight of Làrach an Dùin ruin on the headland build their houses with their doors to the sea and their backs to the broken walls, and will not carry off the good dressed stone lying loose there for the taking, an old woman of that shore saying a wall raised by other hands keeps its own quarrel.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0209"><em>Ceann mhin on the south-eastern shore</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,028</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5525"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,055** — *The smiths of the southern Seann Skell beat out hooks faster than the sea wears them* (Seann Skell). Within a few generations of its resettling, the old harbour of the south becomes the busiest quay on that whole coast, boats going out on every tide and coming home heavy, and its smiths kept at the forge from first light beating out fish-hooks the fishing cannot outlast.
- <a id="ev-EII-5526"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, GE 3,068** — *Achadh shean sinks its well before it breaks a furrow* (Achadh shean). The households returning to the fields cracked by the long drought sink a new well deep into the rock before they plant a single seed, and tell it after as a lesson to their children: dig first, plant after, a well proved in a dry summer being worth more than an early harvest.
- <a id="ev-I-0210"></a>**23 am Màrt, GE 3,079** — *Seann Skell of the south* (Seann Skell). Dia-thìreach households take up the old harbour at the southern Seann Skell and keep its old name. Within a few generations it is the busiest landing on the south coast.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5525"><em>The smiths of the southern Seann Skell beat out hooks faster than the sea wears them</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,055</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5527"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, GE 3,081** — *A boy of Inis mhin is lost among the egg-ledges* (Inis mhin). A boy climbing after eggs is caught by dusk on a shelf below the cliff's highest nests, unhurt but unable to climb either way, and is brought up by torchlight on a rope woven that same night; afterward no one of that settlement works the cliffs alone, two to a rope by custom rather than any law spoken.
- <a id="ev-EII-5528"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, GE 3,100** — *Raonaid born to the king on the eastern shore*. A daughter is born to the king by a wife of the eastern shore and named Raonaid; quick of eye and slow to anger, she will be the half-sister Ìomhar Dearg loves best of all his father's many children, and the hearth he comes home to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0210"><em>Seann Skell of the south</em>, 23 am Màrt, GE 3,079</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5529"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, GE 3,103** — *The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol* (Muileann chaol). When the head of one of the settling households dies, his kin carry stones up the slope above the cattle-fold and raise the first cairn there, one stone laid at a time by whoever had known him; within a lifetime the slope holds as many small heaps of stone as the fold below holds cattle in a good year.
- <a id="ev-I-0211"></a>**21 an Giblean, GE 3,125** — *Achadh shean resettled* (Achadh shean). Households return to Achadh shean after the drought and cut new fields on the higher ground. They sink a deep well first and plant after, and the well does not fail again in this age.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5526"><em>Achadh shean sinks its well before it breaks a furrow</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, GE 3,068</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5530"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, GE 3,140** — *Fearchar Bacach dies at Dùn ìseal*. Fearchar Bacach, who has held Dùn ìseal for the king since he was lamed in the passes long before, dies quietly in his own bed at three thousand one hundred and thirty years of age; his house keeps the hill after him without any household troubling to remark that it is being kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5529"><em>The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, GE 3,103</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5531"></a>**22 an Gearran, GE 3,140** — *Raonaid nic Ailein weds on the eastern shore* (Dùn ìseal). Raonaid nic Ailein, a daughter of the king born to a wife of the eastern shore, marries a herdsman of Fearchar's line from the river-lands below Dùn ìseal, known on that shore better by his flocks than by his name; her house there is afterward the hearth her half-brother Ìomhar Dearg comes back to between his wanderings.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5528"><em>Raonaid born to the king on the eastern shore</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, GE 3,100</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5532"></a>**23 am Màrt, GE 3,161** — *Baile Mòr ruadh settles ground its people call empty* (Baile Mòr ruadh). Households raise a broad red-earthed rise into Baile Mòr ruadh, a morning's walk from the old middens of Seann Dunn, calling the ground around them empty though the middens plainly say otherwise, and dig into nothing of what lies there.
- <a id="ev-I-0212"></a>**20 an Cèitean, GE 3,172** — *Inis mhin settled* (Inis mhin). A few households settle at Inis mhin on the eastern coast. They live by the eggs and birds of the cliffs, and trade feathers inland.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5527"><em>A boy of Inis mhin is lost among the egg-ledges</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, GE 3,081</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5533"></a>**21 an Giblean, GE 3,179** — *A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill*. A shepherd wakes from a sun-warmed sleep to find his whole flock standing stock still along the path worn round Làrach an Teampaill, none grazing, none straying past its edge, and drives them home without letting a hoof cross it, telling after that his sheep had more sense of the place than he did.
- <a id="ev-EII-5534"></a>**20 an Cèitean, GE 3,204** — *Ìomhar is born to the king and called Dearg for his hair*. A son is born to the king in the south and named Ìomhar, called Dearg for hair redder than his father's or his brothers', who grows up about the southern shores and the eastern marches asking, before his first century is out, why a man may not simply be given ground and left to hold it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5533"><em>A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 21 an Giblean, GE 3,179</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0213"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,218** — *Muileann chaol on its hill* (Muileann chaol). Households settle on the hill at Muileann chaol, above the upper reaches of the rivers. Where the library stands now there is a cattle-fold.

## The Years GE 3,251 – 3,500

- <a id="ev-I-0214"></a>**17 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,264** — *Cairns on the hill at Muileann chaol* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). At Muileann chaol a cairn is raised for each head of a household at death, on the slope above the fold. By the end of the age some forty stand there.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5529"><em>The first cairn rises above the fold at Muileann chaol</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, GE 3,103</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5535"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,310** — *Dòmhnall Clachach dies in the north country*. Dòmhnall Clachach, sent north from Dùn ìseal more than three thousand years before and known there only as the stone-cutter's son, dies among people who never troubled themselves with what he had once been, at three thousand three hundred and eight years of age; word of it reaches the hill a full season after the burying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-5534"><em>Ìomhar is born to the king and called Dearg for his hair</em>, 20 an Cèitean, GE 3,204</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0215"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, GE 3,311** — *Baile Mòr ruadh in the east* (Baile Mòr ruadh). Baile Mòr ruadh grows up near the eastern Seann Dunn, on land its people call empty. The middens of Seann Dunn lie a morning's walk away, and the settlers do not dig into them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5532"><em>Baile Mòr ruadh settles ground its people call empty</em>, 23 am Màrt, GE 3,161</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0216"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, GE 3,357** — *The temple ruin avoided* (Làrach an Teampaill). The Dia-thìrich of the eastern hills pass Làrach an Teampaill without stopping and take no stone from it. A path is worn round it at a distance.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-5533"><em>A shepherd's flock will not cross the worn path at Làrach an Teampaill</em>, 21 an Giblean, GE 3,179</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0217"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403** — *Ceann leathan's contests* (Còmhrag Ceann leathan). At Ceann leathan the gathering by the wind-stones ends with wrestling and the lifting of stones. The heaviest, a black boulder, lies on the point still, and few have raised it.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-5536"><em>Alasdair Làidir takes every fall of the contests at three-and-twenty</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-5537"><em>A grey stranger lifts the black boulder at Ceann leathan</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5536"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403** — *Alasdair Làidir takes every fall of the contests at three-and-twenty* (Ceann mhin). At the yearly contests below Clachan nan Gaoth of Ceann leathan, a young herdsman's son named Alasdair Làidir throws every man who stands against him from first light to last, the youngest ever known to do it, and is given by custom the first try at Clach a' Neirt that has never once been raised.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0217"><em>Ceann leathan's contests</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5537"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403** — *A grey stranger lifts the black boulder at Ceann leathan* (Ceann mhin). After Alasdair Làidir's strength fails against it, an unknown grey-haired traveller steps from the watching crowd, sets his hands to Clach a' Neirt and raises it to his knees, then sets it down again gently rather than dropping it, and walks off the headland refusing to give any name the reciters might carry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0217"><em>Ceann leathan's contests</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5538"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,410** — *The tale of the lifted stone wears smooth at other fires* (Seann Skell). Carried from hearth to hearth along the southern coast, the tale of the grey stranger gains, within a few winters, a taller stranger, a one-handed lift and, at one fire near the southern Seann Skell, hands said to glow like a smith's iron, an embellishment Alasdair Làidir spends the rest of his life correcting wherever he hears it repeated.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0217"><em>Ceann leathan's contests</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, GE 3,403</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0218"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, GE 3,450** — *The ford gathering grows* (Fèill Muileann òg). The ford gathering at Muileann òg now draws households from every coast. Its ground is parted by custom: the salt people downstream, the hill people upstream, the flint people on the far bank.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-5539"><em>An old woman at the ford sets a matching tale beside Alasdair's doubted one</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, GE 3,450</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-5539"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, GE 3,450** — *An old woman at the ford sets a matching tale beside Alasdair's doubted one*. At Cruinneachadh an Àtha, crowded that year, an old man past his wrestling years tells, once more, of the stone lifted and gently set down at Ceann leathan; a grey-haired woman at the same fire answers his young doubters not by taking his side but by recalling a near-identical telling she heard thirty years before, from a different mouth entirely, at a fire near the southern Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0218"><em>The ford gathering grows</em>, 3 an Lùnastal, GE 3,450</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0219"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496** — *Stone axes from the north* (Àth àrsaidh). Axes of polished green stone from a quarry near Àth àrsaidh in the north-west are carried all over the island. They are too fine for work; most are laid unused in graves or under house floors.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6000"><em>Ìomhar Dearg wants a green axe for use, not for a grave</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6001"><em>The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6000"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496** — *Ìomhar Dearg wants a green axe for use, not for a grave* (Àth àrsaidh). At a wake in the north-west, Ìomhar Dearg turns over the dead man's green axe before it goes under the turf and asks the son, plainly, for one of his own to carry and use, having buried enough kin himself to want a tool that earns its keep before it earns its grave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0219"><em>Stone axes from the north</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6001"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496** — *The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away* (Àth àrsaidh). An old cutter at the quarry tells Ìomhar Dearg that no green axe was ever cut to be swung, only shown, and that a man wanting an edge for work should go to a common smith and leave the green stone to the graves it is already promised to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0219"><em>Stone axes from the north</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6002"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, GE 3,497** — *Ìomhar's grey axe outlives forty years of use* (Àth àrsaidh). Ìomhar Dearg has a common smith cut him a plain grey axe that same winter, and uses it, reground more than once, for the better part of forty years before the head cracks on a misjudged root and he buries it himself in the ground it first turned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6001"><em>The cutters of Àth àrsaidh turn Ìomhar away</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, GE 3,496</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 3,501 – 3,750

- <a id="ev-I-0220"></a>**13 an Giblean, GE 3,547** — *The quarry at Àth àrsaidh* (Àth àrsaidh). The green-stone quarry at Àth àrsaidh is worked by a few households who trade in nothing else, and the chips about it lie knee-deep. Before the age ends the quarry is forsaken, and the axes cease.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6003"><em>The last cutter of Àth àrsaidh dies without an apprentice</em>, 13 an Giblean, GE 3,547</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6003"></a>**13 an Giblean, GE 3,547** — *The last cutter of Àth àrsaidh dies without an apprentice* (Àth àrsaidh). The seam of true green stone runs thin under every cut the households of Àth àrsaidh try, and the last cutter who still holds the old skill dies that year with no apprentice behind him, his own sons having gone to herding rather than a stone that no longer pays for the teaching.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0220"><em>The quarry at Àth àrsaidh</em>, 13 an Giblean, GE 3,547</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0220a"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, GE 3,588** — *The moor takes the north* (Doire ghlas). The oak falls back, as the pollen in the bog under Doire ghlas shows. Heather, birch and bog-moss spread over the northern lowlands, and the groves that give the north its many Doire names shrink to the sheltered valleys, where they stand yet. In the north this is remembered as the time the winters lengthened.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6004"><em>The oak-groves of the north shrink to the sheltered valleys</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, GE 3,588</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6004"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, GE 3,588** — *The oak-groves of the north shrink to the sheltered valleys* (Doire ghlas). About Doire ghlas and the low ground north of it, heather, birch and bog-moss spread over ground the oak had held unchallenged for longer than any household's reckoning, and the groves that gave the north its many doire-names draw back to valleys the wind cannot reach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0220a"><em>The moor takes the north</em>, 19 an t-Sultain, GE 3,588</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6005"></a>**6 am Màrt, GE 3,610** — *Stepping-stones cross Abhainn fhionn dry-shod*. A household below the willow flats lays flat stones across the shallowest bend of Abhainn fhionn one summer's low water at a time, until within two generations a man may cross the whole width stone to stone in every season but true flood, the first made river-crossing the island has seen.
- <a id="ev-I-0221"></a>**15 am Màrt, GE 3,628** — *The river crossings of Abhainn fhionn* (Abhainn fhionn). Stepping-stones are laid across Abhainn fhionn at its shallows, the first made crossing of any river on the island. They are older than the first bridges, and in places lie beneath them.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6005"><em>Stepping-stones cross Abhainn fhionn dry-shod</em>, 6 am Màrt, GE 3,610</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0222"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680** — *A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol* (Abhainn chaol). A spate on Abhainn chaol takes a party of twelve crossing its fords with salt. Thereafter none crosses there in the wet season.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6006"><em>Twelve are taken at the fords of Abhainn chaol</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6007"><em>Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6006"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680** — *Twelve are taken at the fords of Abhainn chaol*. A spate with no warning a slower rise would have given takes a party of twelve crossing with salt at the fords of Abhainn chaol; five bodies go to their own kin, four unclaimed to the nearest household willing to dig, and three are never found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0222"><em>A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6007"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680** — *Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning*. Word reaches Ìomhar Dearg two days' walk south of Abhainn chaol and he comes as fast as the road allows, arriving to a river already fallen back to its ordinary height and the households of both banks already burying what could be found; no household crosses those fords in the wet season after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0222"><em>A drowning at the fords of Abhainn chaol</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6008"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,703** — *Niall is born to Raonaid on the eastern shore* (Dùn ìseal). Raonaid nic Ailein bears a son on the eastern shore in a colder autumn than the last three running; her half-brother Ìomhar Dearg finds more of her quickness than of his own long line in the child's first evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6007"><em>Ìomhar comes two days too late to the drowning</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 3,680</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0223"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 3,726** — *The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar* (Ceann chiar). The people of Ceann chiar, rebuilding after the Black Wind, set a stone in the midst of their settlement and cut on it a mark for every house lost: twenty-two.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6009"><em>Ceann chiar cuts two-and-twenty marks for A' Ghaoth Dhubh</em>, 12 an Cèitean, GE 3,726</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6009"></a>**12 an Cèitean, GE 3,726** — *Ceann chiar cuts two-and-twenty marks for A' Ghaoth Dhubh* (Ceann chiar). Rebuilding after A' Ghaoth Dhubh that scattered their roofs a generation before, the households of Ceann chiar set a stone in their new-laid houses and cut a plain stroke for every house the wind took, two-and-twenty marks in a row with no names beside them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0223"><em>The Black Wind remembered at Ceann chiar</em>, 12 an Cèitean, GE 3,726</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 3,751 – 4,000

- <a id="ev-I-0224"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 3,771** — *A dry year on the eastern plain* (Muileann bhàn). The rivers of the eastern plain run low for a whole summer, and the households of Dùn ìseal and Muileann bhàn drive their cattle to the warm springs to drink. The shared surplus holds, and no deaths are counted.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6010"><em>A dry summer is answered by the shared surplus</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, GE 3,771</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6010"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 3,771** — *A dry summer is answered by the shared surplus* (Dùn ìseal). The rivers of the eastern plain run so low one summer that Dùn ìseal and Muileann bhàn drive their cattle to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh to drink; the surplus each household had kept against such a year holds long enough that no death is counted for the thirst of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0224"><em>A dry year on the eastern plain</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, GE 3,771</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0225"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,817** — *A second wave on the south coast* (Tonn Mhòr Cnoc chaol). The sea comes in again over the low ground at Cnoc chaol, less far than before. The new houses stand higher on the slope, and none is lost.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6011"><em>A lesser wave comes in at Cnoc chaol</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,817</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6011"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,817** — *A lesser wave comes in at Cnoc chaol*. The sea rises again over the low ground at Cnoc chaol, less far than the wave the coast still tells of; the new houses built higher on the slope since that first wave take no loss, the water finding only empty byres to carry off.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0225"><em>A second wave on the south coast</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,817</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0226"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 3,863** — *The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). The old crack at Cill ghlas moves again, and the spring shifts back uphill. The line of white stones is broken in two places, and is laid again.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6012"><em>The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, GE 3,863</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6012"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 3,863** — *The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again*. The old crack in the ground shifts once more, moving the spring back uphill and breaking the line of white stones that marks the danger in two places; the households walk out with fresh stone and lay the line again exactly as their grandmothers laid it the first time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0226"><em>The ground shakes at Cill ghlas again</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, GE 3,863</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6013"></a>**15 an t-Iuchar, GE 3,900** — *Dùghall born to Ìomhar Dearg*. A son is born to Ìomhar Dearg and named Dùghall, a grave, red-haired child with none of his cousin Niall's laughter in him; Ìomhar, near seven hundred years old, carries him on his wanderings before the boy can walk.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6012"><em>The crack at Gleann na Scoltaidh moves again</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, GE 3,863</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0227"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, GE 3,908** — *Cnoc bheag under the Carragh* (Cnoc bheag). Households settle on the bank of the Abhainn ìseal at Cnoc bheag, a short walk from Carragh Cnoc bheag. They set their houses so that no door faces the stone.
- <a id="ev-EII-6014"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,920** — *Households settle at Cnoc bheag with no door facing the stone* (Cnoc bheag). A generation settles on the bank of Abhainn ìseal a short walk from the standing stone at Cnoc bheag, and sets its houses, by no law anyone can name, so that no door among them faces the stone; every household built after keeps the same pattern unquestioned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0227"><em>Cnoc bheag under the Carragh</em>, 5 an t-Sultain, GE 3,908</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0228"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,955** — *The seal rocks of Inis bhàn* (Inis bhàn). The households of Inis bhàn on the lower Abhainn ìseal take seals from the skerries off the river mouth by agreement, one household to a rock. A rock taken out of turn is the commonest quarrel in their tellings.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6015"><em>Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,955</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6015"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,955** — *Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn* (Inis bhàn). The households by the seal-rocks off the river mouth at Inis bhàn take one rock to a household in its own turn, kept on notched sticks; a rock taken out of turn is the coast's commonest quarrel, settled always by counting the tally aloud rather than raised voices.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0228"><em>The seal rocks of Inis bhàn</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,955</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6016"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, GE 3,960** — *Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own* (Dùn ìseal). Nearly eight hundred years into a wandering right that let him sit at any hearth on the island, Ìomhar Dearg asks the king, on the hill, for ground held in his own name rather than his blood's, wanting a piece of earth that answers to him before it answers to anyone else.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6015"><em>Inis bhàn settles the seal-rocks by the tally of the turn</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,955</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6017"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, GE 3,960** — *The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches* (Dùn ìseal). The king grants Ìomhar Dearg thin-soiled river-grazing between the last settled households and the open country to the east, telling him only that a share given is a share that can be taken back, as every share on the island has been and will go on being.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6016"><em>Ìomhar Dearg asks the king for ground of his own</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, GE 3,960</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6018"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 3,960** — *Ìomhar stands on his own ground looking east* (Dùn ìseal). At the day's end Ìomhar Dearg stands alone on the eastern river-grazing, thin grass under his own feet for the first time in nearly eight centuries of walking ground that answered to another name, and looks east toward country he has not yet walked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6017"><em>The king gives Ìomhar the river-grazing of the eastern marches</em>, 8 an t-Samhain, GE 3,960</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0229"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, GE 4,000** — *Fields at Achadh mhòr* (Achadh mhòr). The wide field at Achadh mhòr, near the warm springs, is cleared and banked, the largest single field of the age. Its bank is laid with the stones of an older wall that no one claims.

## The Years GE 4,001 – 4,250

- <a id="ev-EII-6019"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, GE 4,008** — *Achadh mhòr's wide field is cleared under Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh* (Achadh mhòr). A household near Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh clears and banks the widest single field the eastern country has yet cut from the rough, laying its bank on the stones of an older wall whose builders none of them can name, and grows in a good year wheat enough for three households where before there had been land for none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0229"><em>Fields at Achadh mhòr</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, GE 4,000</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6020"></a>**20 an Gearran, GE 4,021** — *An Cnoc Ruadh's boats come to be kept at Baile ghlas* (Baile ghlas). Boats drawn up in stone and turf sheds at Baile ghlas along the lake shore come, within a generation, to put out oftener than An Cnoc Ruadh's own strand, so that the harbour built beside the hill grows quietly into the hill's chief fishing ground.
- <a id="ev-EII-6021"></a>**22 am Faoilleach, GE 4,034** — *Achadh naomh fences its spring before it raises a house* (Achadh naomh). Settlers at Achadh naomh lead a spring round in channels of their own digging and fence it before a single wall is raised, so that a stranger coming on the place first might take the water, and not the people, for what had been settled there.
- <a id="ev-I-0230"></a>**7 an Cèitean, GE 4,047** — *The harbour at Baile ghlas* (Baile ghlas). The households of the Red Hill draw up their boats at Baile ghlas, along the lake shore from the hill, in sheds of stone and turf. It becomes the fishing harbour of the Red Hill.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6020"><em>An Cnoc Ruadh's boats come to be kept at Baile ghlas</em>, 20 an Gearran, GE 4,021</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6022"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,058** — *Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one* (Caol shean). Rather than let a quarrel over a stretch of river landing run on with no keeper near enough to draw a lot on it, two households of Caol shean sit out a night together and give the ground to the landing itself, for whoever has a boat drawn up there and no other claim; the households are, within two generations, thoroughly mixed by marriage.
- <a id="ev-I-0231"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,091** — *Achadh naomh's spring-fields* (Achadh naomh). Settlers at Achadh naomh in the north water their fields from a spring they will not build over, and lead the water round it in channels. The spring is fenced before any house is.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6021"><em>Achadh naomh fences its spring before it raises a house</em>, 22 am Faoilleach, GE 4,034</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6023"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, GE 4,100** — *Catrìona born of the king's blood* (Dùn ìseal). A daughter of the king's blood is born in the valleys under the hill and named Catrìona; before she is ten she can give a household's line back seven names, and the hill begins to watch her as a valley watches a child who does an ordinary thing early.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0231"><em>Achadh naomh's spring-fields</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,091</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0232"></a>**10 am Màrt, GE 4,128** — *Caol gharbh on the rough strait* (Caol gharbh). Households settle at Caol gharbh on the north-east coast and fish the strait in skin boats. They lay paddles beside their dead.
- <a id="ev-I-0233"></a>**8 an Giblean, GE 4,183** — *Doire chiar* (Doire chiar). A settlement grows up under the dark oaks at Doire chiar in the north. Its people pen pigs in the wood and drive them out to the acorns at the fall of the year.
- <a id="ev-I-0234"></a>**11 am Faoilleach, GE 4,228** — *The river landing at Caol shean* (Caol shean). Caol shean, on the Abhainn ìseal east of the vein, becomes the river landing of the hill households of the east. Salt, fish and seal-skins come up the river to it from the coast, and go on from it into the keepers' country.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6022"><em>Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,058</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6024"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, GE 4,240** — *Ailis is born east of the vein* (Dùn dhearg). A girl named Ailis is born at what will become Dùn dhearg, into a household already turf-cutting for the fort's first bank, and grows up along the ditch's edge hearing, at her own hearth, tellings of a king beyond the vein who does not grow old.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6022"><em>Two households at Caol shean give their disputed landing to no one</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,058</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6025"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, GE 4,250** — *A trader tells Ailis of the gate at Dùn ìseal* (Caol shean). A cloth-trader passing through Caol shean's landing tells the children at a hearth of standing at the very gate of Dùn ìseal and seeing a young-faced man come in at it who has held that hill, by every account at the gate, since before its walls were built; the child Ailis asks whether it does not frighten his own children to grow old beside him, and gets no clear answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6024"><em>Ailis is born east of the vein</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, GE 4,240</a>.</span>

## The Years GE 4,251 – 4,500

- <a id="ev-I-0235"></a>**9 an Gearran, GE 4,274** — *Dùn dhearg raised* (Dùn dhearg). A hill-fort with a double bank is raised at Dùn dhearg, east of the vein, by households who owe nothing to Dùn ìseal. The Stone Kings' list does not name its holders; it says only that Dùn dhearg came not to the gatherings.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6026"><em>The households east of the vein raise the double bank at Dùn dhearg</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 4,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6026"></a>**9 an Gearran, GE 4,274** — *The households east of the vein raise the double bank at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Owing nothing to Dùn ìseal and asking leave of no one, the households of the eastern country dig a deep ditch and raise a double bank at Dùn dhearg, sharing out the labour and afterward the ground within it by households and not by standing, so that the fort itself sets, without any law behind it, the custom the country keeps from then on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0235"><em>Dùn dhearg raised</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 4,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6027"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, GE 4,275** — *A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank* (Dùn dhearg). A family that refuses to send hands to the digging is simply left with its grazing outside the second bank when the ground is drawn, and asks within a generation, of its own accord and under no compulsion, to be let in on the same terms as its neighbours, its late hands reckoned at somewhat less than hands sent early.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0235"><em>Dùn dhearg raised</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 4,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6028"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, GE 4,292** — *Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda*. A son is born in Na Glinn Àrda to a household of Somhairle's line, which keeps Sloinneadh a' Chlachair and takes no share; he will live three hundred and eight years, fewer than his own father, and father Gille-Brìde.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0235"><em>Dùn dhearg raised</em>, 9 an Gearran, GE 4,274</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6029"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, GE 4,304** — *Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg*. A son is born to Dùghall Dearg, son of Ìomhar Dearg, and named Ruairidh, grey-eyed like his great-grandfather the king; Ìomhar holds him at his naming and says the boy will outlive the river-grazing and most of what stands on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6027"><em>A holdout household is left outside Dùn dhearg's second bank</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, GE 4,275</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6030"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, GE 4,310** — *Ailis's husband is buried on the slope above Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). The net-mender of Caol shean whom Ailis married in her twenty-second year dies at Dùn dhearg an old man by any island's reckoning, and is carried out and laid on the slope above the houses with his own net-needle set in the ground at his feet.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6029"><em>Ruairidh born to Dùghall Dearg</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, GE 4,304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6031"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, GE 4,320** — *Seumas born on An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). A son is born in An Cnoc Ruadh's hall and named Seumas; the reciters of the lake shore mark his birth in the roll as they have marked every holder's since Beathag Ruadh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6023"><em>Catrìona born of the king's blood</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, GE 4,100</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6032"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,321** — *Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins* (Dùn dhearg). In her eighty-first year Ailis of Dùn dhearg carries three winters' store of seal-skins the length of the island toward Cruinneachadh an Àtha, meaning to trade them for salt and to stand in the river of the old tellings before her legs fail her; six of that country go with her, the first of Dùn dhearg's people to make the journey.
- <a id="ev-I-0236"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, GE 4,321** — *Dùn dhearg comes to the ford* (Fèill Muileann òg). In the time of Catrìona Mhòr the households of Dùn dhearg come to the ford gathering for the first time, bringing seal-skins and asking for salt. They are given ground of their own on the far bank.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6032"><em>Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,321</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6033"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, GE 4,321** — *The east reaches the ford after five days on the road*. Ailis's party finds households along the road who have never heard of the country east of the vein, and sleeps a night with a family whose grandfather claims a telling, four hands removed, of An Cruinneachadh Mòr held in the three-thousandth year of the Grove; by the fourth day they walk unremarked among a general traffic of salt- and wool-carriers bound the same way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6032"><em>Ailis sets out for the ford with seal-skins</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,321</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6034"></a>**6 an Cèitean, GE 4,322** — *Ìomhar Dearg names the east 'the short-lived' at the ford*. At the fire where Catrìona hears Ailis out, Ìomhar Dearg, holding river-grazing nearby, asks carelessly why ground should be troubled over for people who will all be dead within one of his own lifetimes, and calls them, in that breath, the short-lived; Ailis answers that she has five days' walking behind her and no wish to spend any of what time she has left arguing with a man who will have five centuries to be sorry in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6033"><em>The east reaches the ford after five days on the road</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, GE 4,321</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6035"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,322** — *Young Catrìona gives Dùn dhearg ground at the ford*. Catrìona, of the king's blood and not yet two hundred and twenty-five years old, hears Ailis of Dùn dhearg out at the ford, asks after the double bank and whether it answers to anyone, and gives the eastern households ground of their own on the far bank, this year and every year after, asking no oath in return and receiving none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0236"><em>Dùn dhearg comes to the ford</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 4,321</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6036"></a>**3 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,322** — *Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given* (Dùn dhearg). Ailis's party trades its seal-skins for salt enough to see three households through a hard winter and walks home east of the vein without having sworn anything to the ford or to the hill, and the elders of Dùn dhearg agree, hearing it told, that ground held and no word owed for the holding suits them exactly as it stands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0236"><em>Dùn dhearg comes to the ford</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, GE 4,321</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0237"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,325** — *Settlers at Àth fhiadhaich* (Àth fhiadhaich). Households settle at Àth fhiadhaich in the south-eastern hills, by a ford where wild cattle cross. They take the calves and rear them, and their herds become the best in those hills.
- <a id="ev-EII-6037"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,325** — *Ailis dies on the slope above the double bank* (Dùn dhearg). Ailis dies at eighty-five in her own house on the eastern slope of Dùn dhearg's bank, three years after her one journey to the ford, and is buried beside her husband; her grandchildren keep the tale of the seal-skins and the woman of the king's blood who asked nothing back for the ground she gave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6036"><em>Salt is carried home to Dùn dhearg without any oath given</em>, 3 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,322</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6038"></a>**19 an Giblean, GE 4,327** — *The ford of the wild cattle is settled at Àth fhiadhaich* (Àth fhiadhaich). A household settles a stony crossing in the south-eastern hills where wild cattle come down to drink, and rears the calves born on the near bank apart from the wild herd until, within three generations, that ford's cattle are spoken of the length of the coast as the best in the hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0237"><em>Settlers at Àth fhiadhaich</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,325</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0238"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, GE 4,328** — *Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). Households from the Red Hill settle the point at Ceann àrsaidh on the Abhainn fhionn. They find an old river landing there and name the place for it: the ancient headland.
- <a id="ev-I-0239"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, GE 4,328** — *Cnoc thais in the north-west* (Cnoc thais). Households settle on the damp hill at Cnoc thais in the north-west and drain it with ditches. The ditches carry water still.
- <a id="ev-I-0240"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, GE 4,328** — *Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm in the north-east and live by the fish of its sheltered pools. They build their houses in two rows facing each other, the oldest street on Dia-thìr.
- <a id="ev-EII-6039"></a>**18 an Cèitean, GE 4,330** — *Households build about the old landing at Ceann àrsaidh* (Ceann àrsaidh). People out of An Cnoc Ruadh's country find an old river landing on the Abhainn fhionn, stones set for a boat's keel by hands none living can name, and build their houses about it, naming the place for what they found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0238"><em>Ceann àrsaidh</em>, 17 an t-Sultain, GE 4,328</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6040"></a>**9 am Màrt, GE 4,335** — *Inis mhòr's two facing rows are raised* (Inis mhòr). Households settle Inis mhòr on the Abhainn ghorm and build their houses in two rows facing each other across a single trodden way, so that a neighbour's fire may be borrowed without crossing open ground in the rain; it is the oldest street any teller remembers on Dia-thìr.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0240"><em>Inis mhòr</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, GE 4,328</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0241"></a>**27 an Giblean, GE 4,347** — *Baile gheal in the south-west* (Baile gheal). Baile gheal is founded on the south-western plain round a house with white-limed walls. The lime is burned from the shells of the old middens along the coast.
- <a id="ev-I-0242"></a>**26 an Cèitean, GE 4,347** — *Àth bheag on the eastern coast* (Àth bheag). Households settle the small ford at Àth bheag on the far eastern coast, the easternmost dwelling of the age on the main island. Their boats go out after the geese on the islands.
- <a id="ev-I-0243"></a>**26 an Cèitean, GE 4,347** — *Catrìona Mhòr* (Dùn ìseal). Catrìona Mhòr, twelfth of the Stone Kings and of the king's blood, holds Dùn ìseal under him; hers is the last name in the spoken list. It is told that she knew every household of the hills by its line seven names back.
- <a id="ev-I-0244"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,347** — *Seumas Òg of the Red Hill* (Cathair dhearg). Seumas Òg holds the Red Hill, and with him the spoken list of the Red Hill ends. In the next age what the reciters kept of it is written down.
- <a id="ev-I-0245"></a>**23 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,347** — *The two lists recited together* (Fèill Muileann òg). At the ford gathering, in the time of Catrìona Mhòr, the list of the Stone Kings and the list of the Red Hill are recited one after the other from the first name to the last. It takes from dusk to dawn. For the first time both are heard whole.
- <a id="ev-EII-6041"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, GE 4,347** — *Catrìona takes the hill of Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). Catrìona, of the king's blood and two hundred and forty-seven years old, takes Dùn ìseal formally as the twelfth to hold it of Rìghrean na Cloiche' line, known already for a memory that can give any household's line back seven names without pausing to think.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0243"><em>Catrìona Mhòr</em>, 26 an Cèitean, GE 4,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6042"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, GE 4,347** — *Seumas Òg takes An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). A young man of seven-and-twenty named Seumas takes up the holding of An Cnoc Ruadh his own line has kept since the palisade first burned, the same season Catrìona takes Dùn ìseal; his name will be the last An Cnoc Ruadh's own spoken roll carries.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0244"><em>Seumas Òg of the Red Hill</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6043"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,347** — *The two rolls are spoken whole at the ford in one night*. Eòin gives the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche from Ailean Mòr to Catrìona's own name, and Ùna gives the whole roll of An Cnoc Ruadh from Beathag Ruadh to Seumas Òg's, from dusk to the grey before morning; it is the first time either roll is heard whole, and those nearest the king see him smile when his own name is spoken.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0245"><em>The two lists recited together</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0246"></a>**29 am Màrt, GE 4,350** — *Lots drawn for the slab* (Tobar dhìreach). The lot for the keeper of the slab is drawn now among households from every part of the hills, not only those near the crack. The keepers' house at Tobar dhìreach becomes a place of pilgrimage.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6044"><em>The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills</em>, 29 am Màrt, GE 4,350</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6044"></a>**29 am Màrt, GE 4,350** — *The lot for the slab is drawn from every part of the hills* (Tobar dhìreach). Where the lot for the keeper of the slab was once drawn only from households near the crack, it comes in these years to be drawn from every part of the hills alike, and Tobar dhìreach becomes a place walked to for its own sake by households whose grandparents never heard the crack mentioned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0246"><em>Lots drawn for the slab</em>, 29 am Màrt, GE 4,350</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6045"></a>**4 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,351** — *A nameless hand recuts Calbh Cnoc ghorm*. A hand from Catrìona's own hill goes out to Calbh Cnoc ghorm and recuts its worn grooves along their old lines before the rain can lose them; some who come after hold that a single stroke changed in the recutting, though none can agree which, or prove any changed at all.
- <a id="ev-I-0247"></a>**28 an Gearran, GE 4,353** — *The keepers number nine* (Tobar dhìreach). The keepers of the slab are made nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills. They meet at the slab when a keeper dies, and at no other time.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6046"><em>Luchd-faire na Lice settle at nine</em>, 28 an Gearran, GE 4,353</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6046"></a>**28 an Gearran, GE 4,353** — *Luchd-faire na Lice settle at nine* (Tobar dhìreach). The keepers settle at nine, one drawn by lot for each of nine districts of the hills that no household has ever marked on the ground but every household somehow knows the edge of; the nine meet at the slab only when one of their number dies.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0247"><em>The keepers number nine</em>, 28 an Gearran, GE 4,353</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0248"></a>**9 an Cèitean, GE 4,355** — *Coal in every hearth by the handful*. Every household of the hills burns its handful of the coloured coal, measured in a copy of the stone cup, on one night in the dark of the year, the night later kept as Samhain. All burn at once by agreement, so that the low fires of the handful show on every hillside on the same night.
- <a id="ev-I-0249"></a>**10 an Giblean, GE 4,358** — *A handful refused at Cnoc dhubh* (Cnoc dhubh). The household of the Cnoc dhubh trench, where the two diggers were crushed, refuses its handful of coal for as long as any remembers. No household before it is known to have chosen not to burn at all.
- <a id="ev-EII-6047"></a>**18 an Cèitean, GE 4,358** — *The handful comes to be burned all at once by agreement*. Without any lot or law behind it, every household in reach of another comes to burn its measured handful of an gual dathach on the same dark night, each watching for the first low flame on the nearest hill before lighting its own; the night comes to be called Oidhche na Glaice.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0248"><em>Coal in every hearth by the handful</em>, 9 an Cèitean, GE 4,355</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6048"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, GE 4,358** — *Cnoc na Claise's household refuses its handful* (Cnoc na Claise). The descendants of Torcall Tochlair, who stayed by the trench where his brother was crushed, will not burn the handful with the rest of the hills and give no single answer twice for it; Catrìona sends no one to compel them, and none at the slab asks her to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0249"><em>A handful refused at Cnoc dhubh</em>, 10 an Giblean, GE 4,358</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6049"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, GE 4,360** — *The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots* (Dùn ìseal). Finding she can no longer carry the whole tally of households in her own head, Catrìona sets her people to counting them plainly on a knotted cord, a knot to a hearth, which grows through her years of holding to some nine hundred knots, the largest count made on Dia-thìr in the age; the king's own kin are never upon it.
- <a id="ev-I-0250"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, GE 4,361** — *Counting the households* (Dùn ìseal). The people of Catrìona Mhòr count the households of the hills by knots on a cord, a knot to a hearth. The cord of Dùn ìseal is said to have borne some nine hundred knots, the greatest count made on Dia-thìr in this age.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6049"><em>The cord of Dùn ìseal grows to nine hundred knots</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, GE 4,360</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0251"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, GE 4,364** — *The saying on the column recut* (Calbh Cnoc ghorm). The words on the column at Cnoc ghorm, worn shallow, are recut in their old grooves by a hand from the hill of the Stone Kings. Some later readers hold that the recutting changed a letter; none can prove which.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6045"><em>A nameless hand recuts Calbh Cnoc ghorm</em>, 4 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,351</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6050"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, GE 4,366** — *The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order* (Seann Dunn). A family digging a house-floor into an old midden at Seann Dunn strikes a row of upright stones each cut with a single stroke, knows them for the tally stones of the coast's old people, and sets them back as they lay rather than break them for the floor, building further along the midden's shoulder instead.
- <a id="ev-I-0252"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,367** — *The last Seann-Dhaoine midden disturbed* (Seann Dunn). Households at the eastern Seann Dunn cut into the old midden for a house-floor and find the tally stones. They put them back in the order they lay and build elsewhere.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6050"><em>The tally stones of Seann Dunn are set back in their old order</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, GE 4,366</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6051"></a>**28 an Gearran, GE 4,369** — *The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal*. The custom grows along the south-eastern coast of rowing the newly dead out to Eilean ìseal rather than burying them on the mainland shore, whether learned from the old coast people's graves across the strait or come to of itself; the tellings let the question stand unsettled.
- <a id="ev-I-0253"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,370** — *Eilean ìseal given to the dead* (Eilean ìseal). The households of the south-east coast begin to row their dead to Eilean ìseal, after the old manner of the Seann-Dhaoine. Whether they learned it from the Seann Vell graves on Eilean dhearg, or came to it of themselves, is not told.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6051"><em>The south-eastern coast rows its dead to Eilean ìseal</em>, 28 an Gearran, GE 4,369</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6052"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,370** — *Eilean chrom stays unfished*. No household puts out a boat to fish the waters of Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left with no boat to come back in; his fire was seen three nights running the first year and then no more, and the island stays empty and unfished.
- <a id="ev-I-0254"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,373** — *Gilleasbuig Beag's island* (Eilean chrom). Eilean chrom, where Gilleasbuig Beag was left, stays empty and unfished. His fire is seen on it for three nights, the tellings say, and then no more.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6052"><em>Eilean chrom stays unfished</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,370</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0255"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376** — *The keepers ask to be named* (Fèill Muileann òg). The nine keepers of the slab ask Catrìona Mhòr to declare their charge before the whole ford gathering, so that no king after her may draw the lot at Dùn ìseal. She neither refuses nor agrees, and the matter is left to the next age.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6053"><em>The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6054"><em>Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6053"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376** — *The nine keepers ask Catrìona to declare their charge*. The nine of Luchd-faire na Lice come up together at the ford and ask Catrìona, then in her twenty-ninth year of holding, to declare their charge over the slab, the lot and the handful before the whole gathering so that no king after her may reach for it as Calum Ciar once did; she names the eldest of them by his own line before he finishes bowing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255"><em>The keepers ask to be named</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6054"></a>**9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376** — *Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again*. Catrìona gives the nine keepers neither refusal nor consent, telling them only, "Not this year," and then, before the eldest can press her further, "Ask me again"; the nine go back to their own fires by the slab to wait.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255"><em>The keepers ask to be named</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6055"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, GE 4,380** — *Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other*. Eòin, whose voice carried the whole roll of Rìghrean na Cloiche across one night at the ford, dies in his eightieth year, and Ùna, who answered him roll for roll for An Cnoc Ruadh, follows him within two years in her seventy-third; the telling of that single night passes from then on at second hand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6054"><em>Catrìona answers the keepers: not this year, ask me again</em>, 9 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,376</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6056"></a>**9 an Lùnastal, GE 4,389** — *Catrìona falls ill on the hill* (Dùn ìseal). In her two hundred and eighty-ninth year the sickness comes on Catrìona that will not leave again; she keeps her seat at Dùn ìseal as long as she is able, still able to give a household's whole line back seven names, and the nine keepers, hearing of it, send no word asking again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6055"><em>Eòin Beul-binn and Ùna Ruadh die within two years of each other</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, GE 4,380</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6057"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, GE 4,390** — *Seumas Òg dies on An Cnoc Ruadh* (Cathair dhearg). Seumas Òg, the last name An Cnoc Ruadh's spoken roll carries, dies in his seventy-first year in the winter before Catrìona Mhòr, and the lake shore keeps no holder's fire for him after, only its own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0244"><em>Seumas Òg of the Red Hill</em>, 23 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,347</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6058"></a>**4 am Màrt, GE 4,391** — *The king's kin bring their claims to the hill* (Dùn ìseal). After Catrìona Mhòr's death every soul of the king's blood within three days' walk comes to Dùn ìseal to press a claim on the hill, each able to say the two names of a line whose second name is always Ailean's; the king hears every claim with the same still face.
- <a id="ev-I-0255a"></a>**12 am Màrt, GE 4,391** — *The king takes back the hill* (Dùn ìseal). Catrìona Mhòr dies, and with her the list of the Stone Kings ends. Her kin put forward many claims to Dùn ìseal, and Ailean Mòr gives the hill to none of them. He comes to it himself and holds it in his own hand, as in the first days.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6058"><em>The king's kin bring their claims to the hill</em>, 4 am Màrt, GE 4,391</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6500"><em>The king holds the hill and gives it to none</em>, 12 am Màrt, GE 4,391</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6500"></a>**12 am Màrt, GE 4,391** — *The king holds the hill and gives it to none* (Dùn ìseal). The king tells the gathered claimants that no line among them is better than another and that Catrìona Mhòr's line cannot be handed to a stranger's open palm; he will hold the hill himself, as before Gormshuil first took it up in his name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255a"><em>The king takes back the hill</em>, 12 am Màrt, GE 4,391</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6501"></a>**21 an t-Sultain, GE 4,395** — *The first marriage reckoned openly for a share*. A young man of a minor line is married to a woman three lines removed from the king, and his father says openly at the betrothal fire that the match is made to bring five lines instead of three nearer the front of the reckoning, should the king ever name an heir.
- <a id="ev-EII-6502"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, GE 4,402** — *A daughters' claim disputed at a betrothal*. A household holding good grazing but no claim of its own is joined by marriage to one that claims through four generations of daughters, and the hill argues without settling whether a claim run through daughters weighs more or less than one run through sons.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6501"><em>The first marriage reckoned openly for a share</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, GE 4,395</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6503"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, GE 4,408** — *A betrothal broken over a nearer claim*. A grandmother breaks off her granddaughter's marriage within the month of its making, having found a nearer claim on the groom's own side that she judges would weigh the match's worth downward; the hill takes it as proof that every marriage among the blood is now made for its shares and not for anything else.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6502"><em>A daughters' claim disputed at a betrothal</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, GE 4,402</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6504"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,420** — *A household of the western slopes loses its grazing*. A household that has held grazing on the western slopes eleven generations is told, without reason given, to remove itself to ground of equal size two valleys over before winter; asked directly why, the king says only that a share given has always been a share that can be taken back.
- <a id="ev-EII-6505"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, GE 4,480** — *Raonaid nic Ailein dies at the river-meadow*. Raonaid nic Ailein, the king's daughter, dies at her own river-meadow in her one thousand three hundred and eightieth year; the king sits with her the better part of a day and a night, as he sat once with Gormshuil and once with Somhairle, and speaks of it to no one after.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6504"><em>A household of the western slopes loses its grazing</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,420</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6506"></a>**13 an Gearran, GE 4,480** — *The king takes back Raonaid's grazing*. Within the month of Raonaid nic Ailein's burying the king sends word that the river-meadow grazing is wanted elsewhere and that Niall Òg, her nearest of that line, is to remove his household from it; Niall answers, as he has come to answer every such word, with a laugh.

## The Years GE 4,501 – 4,603

- <a id="ev-I-0255b"></a>**11 an Gearran, GE 4,520** — *Dùn dhearg will not bow* (Dùn dhearg). The king sends to Dùn dhearg and to the households east of the vein, bidding them come in to him. They send his messenger back with nothing, and swear among themselves that they will owe nothing to Dùn ìseal nor to its king. From that year the spears of the east are gathered at Dùn dhearg.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EII-6507"><em>The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6507"></a>**11 an Gearran, GE 4,520** — *The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg* (Dùn ìseal). The king chooses Niall Òg to carry word east of the vein, bidding the households of Dùn dhearg come in to him at last, judging that a man known for asking nothing on his own account is less likely to be mistaken for the leading edge of a conquest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255b"><em>Dùn dhearg will not bow</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6508"></a>**2 an Cèitean, GE 4,520** — *Niall Òg finds Dùn dhearg wanting nothing of the hill* (Dùn dhearg). Niall Òg crosses the vein and finds the double bank of Dùn dhearg larger and better kept than any western telling had prepared him for, its forges and granary proof of a country that has gone far, by its own hands, toward needing nothing from Dùn ìseal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6507"><em>The king sends Niall Òg to Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6509"></a>**1 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,520** — *Fearghal Donn refuses the king's asking* (Dùn dhearg). Fearghal Donn, holder of Dùn dhearg, hears the king's messenger before the whole household and answers that his people have raised their own bank and buried their own dead without any man's leave, and will not be counted among a kin who marry for shares and wait a thousand years for a hill never given.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255b"><em>Dùn dhearg will not bow</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6510"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, GE 4,520** — *Niall Òg carries the refusal home* (Dùn ìseal). Niall Òg rides back to Dùn ìseal and gives Fearghal Donn's word to the king plainly; the king says he had looked for no other answer, thanks him for the carrying of it, and turns to the next claim waiting for him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255b"><em>Dùn dhearg will not bow</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6511"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, GE 4,521** — *The spears of the east are kept to hand* (Dùn dhearg). Word reaches Dùn ìseal by traders, not by any messenger sent for the purpose, that the households about Dùn dhearg have begun keeping their own spears closer than ever before, against a quarrel none of them will name; the king does nothing about it that anyone can see.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255b"><em>Dùn dhearg will not bow</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6512"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,541** — *A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child*. An old woman of Clann na Ceiste, come down from the slab to see the new child, tells Gille-Brìde that a boy born short-lived among the long-lived will learn early what his own kin have never needed to learn until late: how much of a life can be made to matter in however much of it is given.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6028"><em>Gille-Brìde's father born in Na Glinn Àrda</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, GE 4,292</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6513"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, GE 4,543** — *Ceallach is born in Na Glinn Àrda*. A son is born to Gille-Brìde of Somhairle's line in Na Glinn Àrda and is called Ceallach; he is slower to walk and to run than the children before him, the first sign, told back afterward, that the years were coming down faster in him than in his father.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6512"><em>A woman of Clann na Ceiste speaks over the child</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,541</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-I-0256"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, GE 4,550** — *The eve of the Binding*. The handful is kept everywhere in the hills, the keepers are nine, the sharing before the storms is kept on every coast, and the saying is spoken at every gathering. None of it is yet declared, and no oath is yet sworn over the vein. The king holds Dùn ìseal in his own hand, his kin wait about him for their shares, and the spears of the east gather at Dùn dhearg.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6501"><em>The first marriage reckoned openly for a share</em>, 21 an t-Sultain, GE 4,395</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6504"><em>A household of the western slopes loses its grazing</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, GE 4,420</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6506"><em>The king takes back Raonaid's grazing</em>, 13 an Gearran, GE 4,480</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EII-6511"><em>The spears of the east are kept to hand</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, GE 4,521</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6514"></a>**11 an Cèitean, GE 4,570** — *Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Fearghal Donn, who had held Dùn dhearg since before Niall Òg was sent to him and sent back with nothing, dies an old man in his own bed at the fort; the households east of the vein bury him as they buried Ailis, without word sent to the hill and none expected back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6513"><em>Ceallach is born in Na Glinn Àrda</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, GE 4,543</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6515"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,570** — *Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Artair, Fearghal Donn's son, takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg with no more ceremony than his father had used, and says at the burying itself that he will hold what his father held and ask nothing further of the hill until the day it asks something of him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6514"><em>Fearghal Donn dies at Dùn dhearg</em>, 11 an Cèitean, GE 4,570</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6516"></a>**14 am Màrt, GE 4,599** — *Gille-Brìde's father dies in his three hundred and eighth year*. Gille-Brìde's father dies at Samhain in his three hundred and eighth year, fewer years than his own father had, dying as most of that line has learned to die: without illness or wound, simply slower each year until one morning he does not rise from his own hearthstone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6515"><em>Artair takes up the holding of Dùn dhearg</em>, 9 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,570</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6517"></a>**12 an Giblean, GE 4,599** — *Word runs that the kin will gather below Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). At the burying, word runs among the fires that the king's kin mean at last to come down out of their scattered holdings and gather in the valley below Dùn ìseal, each line with its own tents and its own fire, to wait together upon the shares left uncounted since Catrìona Mhòr's death.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255a"><em>The king takes back the hill</em>, 12 am Màrt, GE 4,391</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6518"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, GE 4,601** — *The kin come down household by household* (Dùn ìseal). Through the summer the king's kin come down into the valley below Dùn ìseal household by household and line by line, no single word sent to call any of them, until the valley holds more tents and more fires than any one household has ever seen gathered in one place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0256"><em>The eve of the Binding</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, GE 4,550</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6519"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, GE 4,601** — *Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down* (Dùn ìseal). Murchadh Mòr comes down from the northern plain with a column of sons and grandsons that takes three days to pass any one point on the road, carrying more tent-cloth, it is said, than the valley below Dùn ìseal has ever seen brought to one place at once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6518"><em>The kin come down household by household</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, GE 4,601</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6520"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, GE 4,601** — *Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground* (Dùn ìseal). Eithne comes down from below Làrach an Dùin-fhaire with her own household, and her knot-keeper walks at its head with the household's cord wound about his arm, meaning to be seen keeping count of every soul who sets foot on the new ground, and does so from the first day to the last.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6519"><em>Murchadh Mòr brings his sons and grandsons down</em>, 3 an Dàmhair, GE 4,601</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6521"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, GE 4,601** — *Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein* (Dùn ìseal). Ìomhar Dearg comes down from the eastern marches nursing a hundred years' grievance over river-grazing he judges his by use if not by the king's word, and pitches his tents nearer the vein than any other line thinks wise, exactly, everyone agrees, like him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6520"><em>Eithne's knot-keeper counts every soul on the new ground</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, GE 4,601</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6522"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, GE 4,602** — *Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley* (Dùn ìseal). Sìne nan Snaidhm, knot-keeper of the household cord at Dùn ìseal, walks the growing valley of tents checking each new fire against the cord she carries, so that within a season no soul is pitched there, of the king's blood or of any household following it down, whose count she has not kept.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6521"><em>Ìomhar Dearg pitches nearest the vein</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, GE 4,601</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6523"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, GE 4,602** — *A steward is set over every line* (Dùn ìseal). By the second summer a steward stands over every line camped below Dùn ìseal, holding no ground and no lordship, only charged to speak for its household at the common fires and see its people fed and housed while the waiting goes on, until the valley looks less like a gathering than a town that never raised walls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6522"><em>Sìne nan Snaidhm keeps the cord of the whole valley</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, GE 4,602</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6524"></a>**8 an Cèitean, GE 4,603** — *Sluagh an Ear begins to gather at Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). In the spring Sluagh an Ear begins gathering at Dùn dhearg under Artair, who is said to have waited three years, since he first took up his father's holding, for the very stillness of the hill to break; word of the gathering reaches the western fires within the week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0255b"><em>Dùn dhearg will not bow</em>, 11 an Gearran, GE 4,520</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6525"></a>**30 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,603** — *Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley* (Dùn ìseal). Gille-Brìde walks down out of Na Glinn Àrda with Ceallach, now grown but already, though neither says it, walking more slowly than a man of his years should, and the two stand at evening looking over more fires than either has ever seen gathered at once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6524"><em>Sluagh an Ear begins to gather at Dùn dhearg</em>, 8 an Cèitean, GE 4,603</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6526"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *Sìne nan Snaidhm names Gille-Brìde the one soul asking nothing* (Dùn ìseal). Sìne nan Snaidhm tells Gille-Brìde that his name is on no cord she carries, since he has asked for no ground and no share from anyone, and that he is, that night, the only soul in the whole valley of whom that can be said.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6525"><em>Gille-Brìde and Ceallach come down to see the valley</em>, 30 an t-Ògmhios, GE 4,603</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6527"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household* (Dùn ìseal). Near the end of summer the king comes down from Dùn ìseal with no more than three tents' worth of his own household, going to meet the east himself, while every line camped in the valley says, each at its own fire, that it will follow him within a day or two.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-I-0256"><em>The eve of the Binding</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, GE 4,550</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6528"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The king sends Gille-Brìde home to the hills* (Dùn ìseal). Gille-Brìde asks the king plainly whether he too should come down to the ford; the king tells him to go home to his own people instead, since whatever comes of it will want telling afterward by someone who was not in it, and his line has always been better at the telling than the coming.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EII-6527"><em>The king goes down to meet the east with a handful of household</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EII-6529"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The host of Dùn dhearg musters at the ford* (Dùn dhearg). Every household east of the vein sends its spears down to the river below Dùn dhearg in the last days of an Lùnastal, camping the whole night along a mile of the east bank under Artair mac Fhearghail, meaning to hold the crossing before the king's kin can gather against them.
- <a id="ev-EII-6530"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *Artair mac Fhearghail recalls the answer sent to the king* (Dùn dhearg). At the fires the first night, Artair mac Fhearghail repeats to the host the answer his father Fearghal Donn once sent back with the king's messenger, that the households east of the vein would keep their own bank and owed the hill at Dùn ìseal nothing, and says the answer has not changed in eighty years.
- <a id="ev-EII-6531"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The east finds the king alone at the ford* (Dùn dhearg). At sunrise the host of Dùn dhearg finds a single man sitting on the stone at the head of the ford, his kin nowhere on the far bank; word runs down the fires that the king's own household has quarrelled over the shares of his kingdom and would not follow him east.
- <a id="ev-EII-6532"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The first rush breaks on the king at the ford* (Dùn dhearg). Two hundred spears go into the ford together at sunrise on the first day and are thrown back with the king alone in the water among them; the host sees the river run red below the crossing before the morning mist has fully lifted.
- <a id="ev-EII-6533"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *The east tries the ford's edges and its throwing spears* (Dùn dhearg). Through the first day the host tries the deep channel above and below the ford to come at the king from the side, and by afternoon empties its fletchers' whole store throwing spears from the bank; neither the crossing nor the throwing turns him from his stone.
- <a id="ev-EII-6534"></a>**30 an Lùnastal, GE 4,603** — *A household of Caol shean loses a man to the first day's ford* (Dùn dhearg).
